title: Flaming Lotus Girls - Pulse
imageAlt: Beige circular sticker with intricate white organic coral-like structure and Pulse Flaming Lotus Girls text
description: Pulse is an interactive fire sculpture by the Flaming Lotus Girls, built around an anatomically inspired steel heart that beats fire through its four chambers, its flame effects synced to participants' own heartbeats via biosensors (or triggered manually). Surrounding ribs, LEDs, and lung-like details complete the anatomy. The sculpture debuted at the 3:00 Keyhole at the 2016 Burning Man event and returned to Black Rock City in 2018. This sticker was contributed by Gregg Adams.

title: 2011 Model
imageAlt: Dark vertical sticker with vintage pin-up style woman illustration and Rites of Passage Burning Man 2011 text
description:
The 2011 Burning Man theme, "Rites of Passage," explored the ceremonies and rituals that mark life's major transitions — birth, adolescence, love, grief, death. Across cultures and throughout history, these threshold moments have been recognized as requiring some form of ritual acknowledgment: a deliberate pause to mark the change, to leave one identity behind and step into another. Burning Man itself is often described in exactly these terms: participants arrive as one version of themselves and leave having crossed some invisible threshold.
The pin-up aesthetic Steven Fritz chose for this sticker carries its own set of cultural references — the mid-century American pin-up was a rite of passage in a more ironic sense, a symbol of a particular era's ideals of aspiration and glamour. Reimagined in the context of Burning Man's "Rites of Passage" theme, the retro imagery becomes both homage and interrogation: what do we consider a rite of passage, and what does that choice reveal about us?
This sticker was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2011 event at Black Rock City, Nevada.

title: Lust. Dust. Bacon.
imageAlt: Black and white rectangular sticker with the words Lust, Dust Bacon in white on a black background.
description:
Some stickers tell a story. Lust. Dust. Bacon. tells a philosophy. Three words contributed by Steve Lassoverky from Burning Man 2004 — the year of the Vault of Heaven, when the Man stood atop a geodesic dome Observatory and the Playa was ringed by dioramas of alternate worlds. The weather that year brought dust storms, high winds, and frigid nights.
And yet: the three constants held. The essentials of Black Rock City distilled in order of immediacy — the human impulse, the inescapable environment, and the inexplicable comfort of bacon at sunrise after a night on the Playa.

imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with flaming figure and Black Rock City NY Rites of Passage 2017 text

Sticker from Burning Man's 2011 theme 'Rites of Passage.'
That year's Man balanced atop two pinnacles divided by a chasm, accessible by ladders. Four flaming brazier-topped semi-pyramids surrounded the structure as venues for participant-created rites. BRC streets ran from Anniversary to Liminal.

The camp's pyro-laser-equipped aircraft became part of the visual landscape of that year's Playa, sitting near the Raygun Gothic Rocket installation.

title: Axis Mundi — Burgundy
imageAlt: Circular sticker: a geometric tile mandala in blues, yellows, greens, and pinks, burgundy border. Text: Burning Man 2026, Axis Mundi, Black Rock City
description: Clark Stoeckley designed this mandala series for 2026, channeling the Burning Man theme's "cosmic, centering energy" into Islamic geometry-inspired patterns. He gifted 500 sticker packs — these mandalas paired with humorous and political stickers — to burners across Black Rock City, calling the reactions when people opened them one of his favorite moments of the Burn. Stoeckley is a repeat Burning Man muralist (work on the playa in 2009, 2010, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2022, and 2024) and a longtime geometric abstract painter, currently an Associate Professor of Art & Graphic Design at the American University of Kuwait.

title: Pack it in pack it out
imageAlt: Pack It In Pack It Out sticker. Two vans on playa arriving full of gear, leaving exhausted. Text: Black Rock City 10 Principles, Leave No Trace. 2019.
description:
Leave No Trace is one of Burning Man's 10 Principles — and Pack It In Pack It Out is how it works in practice. 
Everything you bring to Black Rock City comes back out with you: every wrapper, every bottle cap, every strand of MOOP. The Playa gives you everything and keeps nothing. 
Jamen Percy — the creator behind the Safety Third sticker — made this principle into a sticker in 2019 during the Metamorphoses burn. A simple message that every Burner knows before they arrive, and truly understands by the time they leave.

title: Burning Man 2007
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with white geodesic structure illustration and Burning Man 2007 Back to Basics text
description:
The Green Man. That was the 2007 Burning Man theme — humanity's relationship to nature, the environment, the planet we are currently dismantling at speed. The official poster was designed by Dominic Tinio. The Earth Guardians volunteer group distributed thousands of Greening Man stickers across the Playa, part of a year when environmental consciousness was embedded into the event's central narrative.
The 2007 sticker carries the visual language of that year: green energy, ecological urgency, the idea that Burning Man could model something about how humans might exist differently on the planet. Whether it succeeded is a debate the community has been having ever since. The sticker is from the year the conversation started in earnest.

title: The Playa Was on Fire

title: Beyond Belief
imageAlt: Black sticker with yellow Beyond Belief 2003 stylized text and standing figure silhouette
description:
The 2003 Burning Man theme was Beyond Belief — an invitation to explore the space where spirituality, metaphysics, faith, and doubt collide.
Participants were encouraged to build labyrinths, create temples, host ritual processions, and inundate the Playa with sacred spaces. Over 120 art installations answered that call.
The official sticker from that year carries the weight of a question Burning Man has always asked: what do you believe when you're standing in the middle of the desert with 30,000 other people, watching something burn?

title: BRC
imageAlt: White oval sticker with BRC in ornate gothic lettering in European car sticker style
description:
Black Rock City — the temporary municipality that Burning Man assembles each year in the Black Rock Desert of Nevada — is in many respects a fully functioning city. At its peak, it houses more than 70,000 residents and operates its own radio stations, medical services, airport, post office, and civic infrastructure. During its brief existence, it briefly ranks among the largest cities in Nevada.
The oval sticker format is immediately recognizable as the international vehicle identifier used across Europe, where drivers affix oval badges bearing country codes when crossing borders — "F" for France, "GB" for Great Britain. Applying this convention directly to BRC frames Black Rock City as a destination equal in legitimacy to any nation-state. The gesture is affectionate but pointed: the community that Burning Man creates is, in many respects, more deliberately designed than most cities, and its citizens are deeply committed to it.
This sticker was contributed by Courtney Driver for the 2010 "Metropolis: The Life of Cities" event year, a theme that invited reflection on what cities are, how they function, and what Black Rock City reveals about the possibilities of urban life.

title: Thanks Larry
imageAlt: Round black sticker with sepia portrait of Larry Harvey in cowboy hat and sunglasses, "THANKS LARRY" in bold text along the bottom edge.
description:
Larry Harvey co-founded Burning Man in 1986 — a bonfire on Baker Beach with a small group of friends. Over three decades he shaped Black Rock City into a temporary metropolis of 80,000 and wrote the 10 Principles, the philosophical framework used by Burning Man communities worldwide.
He died on April 28, 2018, four months before that year's burn. Jamen Percy contributed this sticker to the Archive in 2022, the year Black Rock City returned after two years of pandemic cancellations.
Two words. That's all it takes.

title: Talk To God
imageAlt: Blue circular “Talk to God” logo with white text, red icon, and outer ring reading “TalkToGodVirtual.com,” “Since 2003,” and “Black Rock Bell Co.”
description:
The first Talk to God phone booth installation was created by members of the Ojai Bureau of Pleasure (OBOP) in 2003. Beyond Belief was the theme of the burn that year.
The idea was simple: would you like to talk to God? What came of the idea is one of the longest running art installations existing on the Playa. No one knows how many calls were answered, but many remember the experience from either side of the line.

Back to the Friend Zone is the kind of 2025 Burning Man camp where strangers become friends fast — because everyone who shows up already gets the joke. Camp sticker as icebreaker: show up, collect the sticker, and you are already part of the bit.

title: Make Black Rock City Great Again!
imageAlt: White text 'MAKE BLACK ROCK CITY GREAT AGAIN!' in a red-bordered rectangle with red stars top and bottom, on a navy blue background.
description: This parody sticker borrows the cadence of a familiar campaign slogan and points it squarely at Black Rock City, playing into Burning Man's long tradition of Playa humor and homemade political-satire art. Anonymous, self-made joke stickers like this one have circulated among Burners on the Playa for years — part of the city's DIY, unbranded sticker culture.

title: Burner Robot
imageAlt: Dark square sticker with cartoon robot amid flames and BRC 2018 Burner Robot Is Ready to Burn text
description:
The 2018 Burning Man theme was I, Robot — an exploration of artificial intelligence, automation, and what it means to be human in a world where the line between person and machine is getting harder to see. The Man base that year was designed around humanity's complicated feelings about algorithmic intelligence and cybernetic augmentation. The official call for sticker designs that year specifically invited robot-inspired submissions.
Burner Robot answers that call directly: a robot who burns. Or maybe a burner who is also a robot. At Burning Man, where people wear costumes that blur identity and reality, the distinction matters less than you'd think. The sticker came through the community design process and ended up in the catalog — a small metal ambassador from the machine year.

title: I got Buzz-ed
imageAlt: Dark sticker with Buzz Aldrin photo and I Got Montclairs Man on the Moon Buzz-ed BM2K3 Burning Man 2003 text
description: Burners visiting the Schwenkers' Chapel of Buzz, in Snowflake Village, got stickers commemorating Buzz Aldrin's Apollo 11 moon trip in 1969. The graphic is from the Buzz Banner, which hung over the Buzz parade route in Monclair, NJ.

title: Temple of Whollyness
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with all-seeing eye triangle design and Temple of Whollyness 2013 text in cosmic style
description:
The Temple of Whollyness rose from the Playa in 2013 as the largest interlocking wood structure ever built at Burning Man — an 87-foot-square pyramid, 64 feet tall, assembled from thousands of precisely cut puzzle pieces without a single nail, screw, or drop of glue.
Designed by Gregg Fleishman, Melissa "Syn" Barron, and Terry Gross, the structure held together through geometry alone. Like all Burning Man temples, it served as a place of grief, gratitude, and release — and like all of them, it burned.
This sticker, contributed by Steven Fritz, carried its eye out into the world.

title: Burning Man 2020 Canceled
imageAlt: Round sticker with bold red CANCELED stamp over Burning Man 2020 The Multiverse badge
description:
This sticker was designed during the early weeks of COVID, when the necessities of the pandemic — toilet paper, masks — had become the defining symbols of a world in crisis. The creator took the Burning Man logo and wrapped it in those symbols: TP and mask applied directly to the iconography of the event. Then they printed it and started sending copies to other burners.
Burning Man 2020 was canceled. In its place came Multiverse, a virtual event. But this sticker is not about the virtual event — it is about the moment of cancellation, the specific absurdity of losing the burn to a pandemic. It is a document of a very strange year, made by someone who needed to make something about it and then give it away.

title: Poop Clear
imageAlt: White script wordmark 'poop clear' above 'COLONOSCOPY CAMP' and 'BURNING MAN 2026,' on a black background.
description: PoopClear — labeled Colonoscopy Camp on the sticker itself — turns the pre-colonoscopy 'clear liquid' bowel-prep diet into a classic piece of Burning Man toilet humor, a genre with deep roots on the playa given how central, and how discussed, sanitation always is at Black Rock City. It's the kind of homemade, camp-made joke sticker that circulates informally long before anyone thinks to catalog it.

title: It was already ON FIRE when I got here.
imageAlt: Red square sticker with white text reading “It was already on fire when I got here.”
description: This sticker, "It was already ON FIRE when I got here," was submitted by Dima for the 2025 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Tomorrow Today theme. Specific design details haven't been documented yet.

title: Stag Camp
imageAlt: Orange sticker with skull and deer antlers illustration and Stag Camp Burning Man 2009 text
description:
Stag Camp is a Burning Man theme camp created for solo burners arriving to BRC without an existing camp affiliation.
Founded around 2007, it grew from a small core group into a community of 50+ travelers who share shade and look out for each other while remaining fully independent on the Playa.

title: DMV - Mutant
imageAlt: White oval sticker with Mutant BRC-DMV 2000 text in European car sticker style
description: This sticker represents the Department of Mutant Vehicles (DMV), Burning Man's official program for licensing and regulating the art cars and mutant vehicles permitted to roam Black Rock City. It dates to the 2000 event, held under that year's official theme, The Body.

title: Fuck Your Burn
imageAlt: Circular sticker with Hamsa hand with raised middle finger and Fuck Your Burn BLM 2019 text
description:
"Fuck Your Burn" is a phrase with specific cultural currency in the Burning Man community — a pushback against the gatekeeping and one-upmanship that can emerge when any community develops its own internal hierarchies of authenticity. It targets anyone who claims their experience of the event is more real, meaningful, or legitimate than others': veterans who dismiss newcomers, purists who mourn the event's growth, anyone who treats their relationship to Burning Man as a credential.
The phrase is rooted in Burning Man's principle of radical inclusion — the conviction that no participant's experience is more valid than another's. As the event grew from a small counterculture gathering to an internationally attended phenomenon, debates about authenticity intensified, and "Fuck Your Burn" emerged as the community's sharpest corrective: a reminder that the burn belongs to everyone who shows up.
This sticker was contributed by Chris for the 2019 event year.

title: Gypsy Kitties
imageAlt: Colorful circular sticker with decorative cat face and mandala pattern and Gypsy Kitties BRC 2014 text
description: This Gypsy Kitties camp sticker was created by fingerwave and gifted at the 2014 Burning Man event, held under that year's Caravansary theme.

title: Terra Incognita
