description: Terra Incognita was created by Erin for 2021, before Burning Man's theme for that year was finalized as The Great Unknown — Erin's own working title, kept as a "Limited Edition" sticker.

title: And Who Are You?
imageAlt: Square sticker with illustrated caterpillar wearing top hat and And Who Are You Burning Man 2023 text
description:
This year I canceled Burning Man and decided just shortly before (4 days before) to go! It’s my fourth burn and the first last minute and first free camping burn.
This sticker is my last second Playa gift this year, the design was in my head since Burning Man published the Theme for 2024 "Curiouser and Curiouser" which is linked to Alice in wonderland… and as you all know the worm smoking a hookah and asking Alice "AND WHO ARE YOU?" "AND WHO ARE YOU?" "AND WHO ARE YOU?" you know now the story behind my sticker design.

title: Da Vinci’s Workshop
imageAlt: White circular sticker with Vitruvian Man mechanical figure and Da Vincis Workshop Burning Man 2016 text
description: Created by James Wickham and contributed by Ralph Boethling, this Da Vinci's Workshop design incorporates symbols representing Burning Man's Ten Principles and was submitted to the Burning Man Project (BMORG) for its official sticker contest for the 2016 event.

title: Web of Wyrdsssss
imageAlt: Round holographic sticker with Burning Man figure and geometric web design and Burning Man Tomorrow Today 2025 text
description: Web of Wyrdsssss was Rory Kalmar's gate sticker submission for the 2025 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Tomorrow Today theme.

title: BRC Municipal Airport – Year?
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with orange Black Rock City Municipal Airport text and airport crosshair symbol
description:
Black Rock City has a real airport. FAA identifier 88NV. Two 6,000-foot runways scraped into the dry lakebed. On busy arrival days it ranks among the hundred busiest airports in the United States. Burning Man has welcomed pilots since 1991, when early aviators simply landed wherever they judged best and the city grew up around their planes. The airport was formally founded in 1999 by pilot Lissa Shoun, and by 2004 it had an official manager, facilities team, and volunteer coordinator.
The sticker's exact year is unknown — the catalog records it as 2012, but it could be earlier or later. What is certain is that someone made an airport sticker for a city that only exists for one week a year, which is exactly the kind of detail that makes Black Rock City feel completely real.

title: Serendipitea
imageAlt: Holographic circular sticker with vibrant swirling iridescent rainbow design
description:
"I Am From Hamburg in Germany and I belong to Camp Serendipitea.

This dreamy Sticker I created is a combination out of our pre burn party banner in May 2022 and pictures taken by me at the burn 2019 In BRC.“ - Sophie Graubner

title: Lamplighters
imageAlt: Round white sticker with black lantern illustration and red accents, with circular text “LL BRC NV – Celebration Illumination Navigation”.
description: This sticker, contributed by burnman, promotes the Lamplighters — the volunteer guild that has lit Black Rock City's night-time lamps for over three decades, processing through the city each evening in traditional robes to hang kerosene lanterns on spires. It's dated to the 2001 Burning Man event and that year's Seven Ages theme.

title: Dolly Llamas 2024
imageAlt: An illustrated llama's face and neck with a blonde curly perm, and red lips, wearing a striped orange, red, and green tank top.
description: Dolly Llamas is a Burning Man theme camp, serving southern hospitality in the high desert since 2022. The camp takes its name — and its glamour — from Dolly Parton, reimagined here as its mascot llama, big blonde curls and all. A wink at one of music's most beloved icons, made by Burners who wanted a little of her sparkle out on the playa.

title: Burner State of Mind
imageAlt: Dark rectangular sticker with stylized orange and white Burner State of Mind typography
description:
In 2020, the in-person Burning Man did not happen. What did happen was that tens of thousands of people who had been building their lives around the event for years had to find out what Burning Man meant to them when there was no Playa to go to. This sticker answers that question with a phrase that had been floating around the community for years but felt newly urgent: it is a state of mind.
Burner State of Mind is an identity claim that does not depend on tickets, weather, or a functioning calendar year. It says the values — radical self-reliance, gifting, communal effort, leaving no trace — exist in you regardless of whether the city currently exists in the desert. The burn is wherever you are.

title: Dr. MegaVolt
imageAlt: Dr. MegaVolt sticker. Black background. Stylised "M" logo in red and blue with lightning bolts. Text: Dr MegaVolt™. Burning Man 2010.
description:
Austin Richards has been standing inside lightning bolts at Burning Man since 1998.
A particle physicist with a PhD from UC Berkeley, he built his first Faraday suit in 1997 — constructed from a birdcage, heating duct, and flexible dryer duct — and Dr. MegaVolt was born. Performing with a double Tesla coil mounted on a truck and generating 40-foot arcs of electricity at up to one million volts, Dr. MegaVolt is one of Black Rock City's most iconic and longest-running art acts.
Steven Fritz contributed this sticker to the Archive in 2010.

title: This Is Your Brain on Playa
imageAlt: Round sticker with cartoon brain with googly eyes on colorful mandala and Burning Man Black Rock City 2017 text
description:
When I would meet people and we'd chat a bit, I'd ask if they would like a sticker, and then I'd hand them this and say, "This is your brain on Playa".
In subsequent years I made the same sticker with a different color theme. There were a few people I met who had a sticker from a previous year. Hot dog! - Adam Patch

title: Not Today JohnRey!
imageAlt: Black rectangular sticker with white text reading "Not Today, JohnRey" in a bold serif-adjacent font.
description: An affectionate inside joke among the 2026 Rampart crew.

title: Faces of Burning Man
imageAlt: Round sticker with flaming eye design in red orange and green colors
description: This sticker was gifted by Shane, who runs the @faces_of_burningman Instagram project — part of the long-running "1000 Faces of Burning Man" portrait series — and was designed by his son for the 2024 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Curiouser & Curiouser theme.

title: Areola 51
imageAlt: Sticker reading “Areola 51” featuring a UFO hovering above stylized desert hills, framed by a large semicircular stone-textured arc.
description:
The Areola 51 sticker marks the 2025 debut of one of Black Rock City's newest theme camps, whose name riffs on the real Area 51 — the classified Air Force facility in the Nevada desert whose decades of official secrecy turned it into pop-culture shorthand for UFOs, aliens, and government cover-ups. 
That kind of pun is a Burning Man tradition: camps build their names, their art, and their culture around a joke, then invite the rest of the city in on it. Areola 51 contributed this design themselves as part of the 2025 event, held under the theme Tomorrow Today, which asked participants to imagine — and start building — better futures instead of just waiting for one to arrive. 
For a first-year camp, adding a sticker to the Archive is its own small version of that idea: showing up, staking a claim on playa history, and writing yourself into the record."

title: Tarotist Training Camp
imageAlt: Pink square sticker with photograph and Tarotist Training Camp Year Center Camp 2008 Burning Man text
description: Tarotist Training Camp's sticker was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2008 Burning Man event, the year of the festival's American Dream theme.

title: Disco Gazebo
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with colorful dancing figures and Camp Disco Gazebo Burning Man Multiverse 2020 text
description: Sticker created for 2020 unBurn, Disco Gazebo is a playhouse raised as a gazebo by TARDIS that lived in my front yard for the Home Burn and has now returned to the Stars. My first Gifting Guild offering.

title: Tree Evolution
imageAlt: Vertical rectangular sticker with stylized tree illustration and Tree Evolution 2007 text
description: Tree Evolution was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2007 Burning Man event, staged under that year's The Green Man theme — fitting company for a piece built around a tree motif.

title: Beethen ArtCar
imageAlt: Holographic iridescent sticker with detailed illustrated bee on rainbow metallic background
description:
Art cars are the heartbeat of Black Rock City after dark — rolling sculptures that move through the Playa carrying sound systems, fire rigs, and the people lucky enough to be aboard.
Beethen ArtCar is one of those rolling dreams. Creator Michael mailed this sticker directly to the catalog — a personal act of gifting that fits the spirit of BRC perfectly.
Two versions exist, which is to say: the story was still unfolding. Catch it on the Playa if you can.

title: Bangers Only
imageAlt: Black-and-white porta-potty with a sunburst behind it, a swirling eye on the door, and a martini glass beside it.
description:
Camp Bangers Only's porta-potty isn't what it looks like: open the door and you're actually walking into a hidden speakeasy built inside two shipping containers, complete with a proper bar, HVAC, and (allegedly) Vegemite toast. 
The camp carries on the 17-year legacy of Camp Bang Bang under a new name and a blunt tagline — "No buns. No sauce. Bangers. Only." Portal Potty is the wink at their own best-kept secret.

title: Quickie Mart
imageAlt: Red and teal sticker in convenience store logo style with Cameltopia Quickie Mart Under New Same Old Mis-Management text
description: Quickie Mart was also designed by Clark / This Motherfucker for Cameltopia theme camp at the 2024 Burning Man event, the same Curiouser & Curiouser theme year as its camp-mate sticker, Joe.

title: Have you seen this cat?
imageAlt: Photo sticker with tabby cat and Have You Seen This Cat Burning Man 2023 Black Rock City text
description: Have You Seen This Cat?, created by Clark / This Motherfucker for the 2023 Burning Man event, plays on the familiar "lost pet" flyer format — a fitting joke for the year of the festival's animal-themed Animalia.

title: St. Alice's Valentine's Restaurant Day Sticker Swap
imageAlt: Dark hexagonal sticker with St Alices Valentines Restaurant Day 2021 Sticker X Massacre text with hearts
description: Scott created this sticker for Camp Balls' St. Alice's Valentine's Restaurant Day sticker swap, giving a copy to every participant in the February event — an annual tradition also held in 2022. It's dated to 2021, the year Burning Man's Black Rock City gathering moved online under The Great Unknown theme.

title: Camp Balls- Herd Immunity
imageAlt: Colorful sticker with cartoon pony characters and Herd Immunity The Great Undying text in My Little Pony style
description: Sparkle Pony Herd Immunity is a 2.5" x 5" glitter card from Camp Balls' 2021 Glitter Card series, made by Scott for the 2021 Burning Man event — the second consecutive year Black Rock City's gathering moved online, staged as The Great Unknown.

title: Everything Is Virtual
imageAlt: White rectangular sticker with dense repeated virtual text and Burning Man stick figure in center
description: Created by Shana for the 2020 Burning Man event, this sticker marks the year Black Rock City had to be "built virtually" rather than in the Nevada desert, after the physical gathering was cancelled due to COVID-19 and reimagined as the Multiverse.

title: Raygun Gothic Rocket
imageAlt: Raygun Gothic Rocket sticker. Orange circle. White rocket silhouette with orbiting dots. Text: raygungothicrocker.com. Burning Man 2009.
description:
The Raygun Gothic Rocketship launched onto the Playa at Burning Man 2009 as one of the most ambitious art projects in the event's history. 
Built by artists Sean Orlando, Nathaniel Taylor, and David Shulman with a crew of 85 artists, engineers, and fabricators, the 50-foot, 20,000-pound steel and brushed aluminium rocket was a full-scale retro-futurist vision straight out of a 1950s sci-fi dream. Attendees could climb a gantry and walk through three interior decks, complete with aliens in tubes. 
After Burning Man, the rocket toured the San Francisco Bay Area before finding a permanent home outside the Wings Over the Rockies Air and Space Museum in Denver, Colorado. Steven Fritz contributed this sticker to the Archive in 2009.

title: Animalia Wolf
imageAlt: Silver holographic sticker with a geometric wolf face and “2023” at the top, reflecting rainbow light.
description:
Burning Man's 2023 theme, Animalia, invited Black Rock City to explore its own place inside the animal kingdom — real animals and mythic ones, from the trickster Coyote of Native American tradition to the sacred beasts of ancient Egypt. 
At its center was tonalism, the old belief that every person carries an animal counterpart tied to who they are. 
Wolves have long stood in for that kind of bond across cultures — loyalty, pack, wildness held together — making one a natural choice to represent the theme. Dima contributed this wolf sticker to the Archive in 2023, though its fuller backstory has never been recorded.

title: BMIR KFAT
imageAlt: Colorful sticker with cartoon cowboy DJ character and BMIR 94.1 Black Rock City Nevada text
description:
Rocky makes an annual BMIR sticker as a homage to legendary American radio stations — and KFAT is one of the legends.
KFAT 94.5 FM broadcast from Gilroy, California between 1975 and 1983, playing what it called a high-cholesterol mix of country, blues, zydeco, rockabilly, bluegrass, novelty 78s, Hawaiian, folk, and pretty much anything else it felt like. The station's loyal listeners called themselves Fatheads. Its spirit carried forward into KPIG.
Combining BMIR with KFAT is a tribute to two stations that refused to be normal.

title: The Secret Gentlemen's Club
imageAlt: Yellow circular sticker with robotic figure and Burning Man 2018 I Robot text
description: This oval sticker was created by Jim for The Secret Gentlemen's Club theme camp, featuring a robot wearing the camp's official logo — fitting for the 2018 Burning Man event's I, Robot theme.

title: We Will Dance Again
imageAlt: Holographic star-shaped sticker with geometric mandala pattern and small text around the edges reading “We will dance again” and “Burning Man 24.”
description: This sticker, "We Will Dance Again," was submitted by Dima for the 2024 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Curiouser & Curiouser theme. Specific design details haven't been documented yet.

title: Burner on Board
imageAlt: Yellow sticker with robot figure and BURNER ON BOARD 2008 text, parody of Baby on Board signs
description:
This sticker was designed for the default world — meant to be placed on your car after you drive back from Black Rock City and re-enter everyday life. It is a riff on the Baby on Board window signs that were everywhere in the 1980s and 90s, but the message is different. Not a warning about a vulnerable passenger. A declaration about the driver.
The 2008 Burning Man theme was American Dream, and this sticker fits that energy perfectly: taking an iconic piece of American roadside culture and running it through a Burning Man filter. It signals to other burners that you exist in the default world but belong somewhere else. A quiet wink at a hundred miles per hour.

title: Sandworms
imageAlt: Dark teal circular sticker with psychedelic worm and paisley pattern and Waking Dreams text
description: Sandworms, designed by Jacqueline Han, was selected by the Burning Man organization itself to be printed and distributed to theme camps for gifting during the 2022 event, staged under that year's Waking Dreams theme.

title: Taxis Mundi
imageAlt: Illustration of a white MASH-style ambulance with a red stripe, blue Star of Life symbol, and the words “Taxis Mundi” on its side.
description:
Taxis Mundi is a 2026 Burning Man sticker for ESD (Emergency Services Department), the theme camp running Black Rock City’s medical operations. 
Created by Sparklecorn, the design puns “Axis Mundi” into a MASH-style ambulance for some low-hanging-fruit theme-camp humor.

title: Burn Clean
imageAlt: Dark hexagonal sticker with circular radar chart design and Burn Free 2018 text in white
description:
Burning Man has a sobriety culture that often goes unnoticed by people who assume the event is entirely about intoxication. Burn Clean is for the sober burners — people who experience the Playa, the art, the community, the burning of the Man, all of it, without substances. It turns out that a glowing city in the middle of the desert, lit by fire and full of strangers who treat you like family, is pretty overwhelming on its own.
The 2018 theme was I, Robot — a look at where the line falls between human and machine, presence and automation. Burn Clean carries that energy in a specific direction: nothing automatic about showing up fully present, wide awake, and completely yourself. The sticker exists to say: we are here too.

title: BM 2020 WTF?
imageAlt: Heart-shaped sticker with illustrated figures and BM 2020 WTF text in dark lettering on light background
description:
Sebastian designed this and colored it digitally during the strangest year in Burning Man history.
The 2020 burn was canceled due to COVID-19 — the first time the event had not happened since 1997. In its place came Multiverse, a virtual event. The sticker exists in both round and square versions, because when a global pandemic cancels your plans and you decide to make art about it anyway, you might as well go in both formats.
WTF feels like the appropriate editorial response.

title: Coat of Arms
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with US presidential eagle coat of arms design and Burning Man 2008 text
description:
This sticker was chosen as the "official" sticker for 2008. Produced by the org and gifted to everyone who went through the gate.
Halcycon -  "I took an official US logo image of an eagle with arrows and branches and replaced the head with the Man and made the eagle holding torches". 
Halcycon - "The best story I've heard about this sticker is that a consultant working in Afghanistan once used this sticker to get through an official checkpoint (since it looked so "official.")"

title: Camp Upsie Dasium
imageAlt: Photo sticker with two Mona Lisa figures wearing sunglasses and BRC 2016 Camp Upsie Dasium You a Mann text
description: This Camp Upsie Dasium — also known as Camp GravyBrain — sticker, contributed by Captain Danger, was named "The Mona Larry," a nod to Da Vinci's Workshop, Burning Man's official theme for 2016.

title: Carnival of Mirrors
imageAlt: Circular Burning Man 2015 “Carnival of Mirrors” gate sticker with red and yellow concentric rings and radiating compass-like design.
description:
A variant sticker from Burning Man's 2015 art theme 'Carnival of Mirrors,' which explored how modern media and self-image distort reality and perception.
The Man stood within a mirrored pavilion and funhouse structure. Multiple sticker editions were produced for this theme.

title: DREAM (dust rules everything around me)
imageAlt: Yellow circular sticker with black Burning Man figure and Burning Man Dream Dust Rules Everything Around Me text
description: Created by Kelly for Killadelphia camp, this design plays on the Wu-Tang Clan logo and its famous "C.R.E.A.M." phrase, reworked as "dust rules everything around me." Scott Whitaker helped digitize the artwork for the 2021 Burning Man event, the second year the festival's gathering moved online, themed The Great Unknown.

title: Temple of Joy
imageAlt: White sticker with architectural illustration of Temple of Joy structure and Temple of Joy Burning Man 2002 text
description: The Temple of Joy was the official 2002 Temple at Burning Man, designed and built by David Best. Best had built Black Rock City's very first Temple, the Temple of the Mind, alongside Jack Haye in 2000, establishing what became an annual tradition: a space set apart from the celebratory burning of the Man, meant for grief, remembrance, and quiet reflection.

title: Manifest Destiny
imageAlt: Dark square sticker with grid of geometric symbols and Manifest Destiny 2008 text repeated twice
description: Manifest Destiny, created by Shanan Bentley in yin-and-yang versions, carries the message that the spirit of Black Rock City "should be done everywhere." It's dated to the 2008 Burning Man event, held under that year's American Dream theme.

title: Next Year
imageAlt: Purple and teal square sticker with large Next Year text in clean minimalist typography
description: Next Year was gifted by fingerwave at the 2014 Burning Man event, the year of the festival's Caravansary theme.

title: Evolve
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with diamond shapes and EVOLVE Burning Man text with heart and skull designs
description: Evolve III, contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2009 Evolution-themed event, credits CameraGirl for supplying many of the stickers in this particular series.

title: B&A
imageAlt: Circular holographic sticker: dripping "B" and "A" letters flank an X-shaped emblem with a heart center, ringed by red flames.
description:
"This was our 1st year together at Burning Man!! We had both been in previous year 2012 was Amber last year and 2011 for me!! 
We finally made it back Home in 2026!! This is the sticker of Camp BA". — Buddy.

title: HELIX
imageAlt: Dark sticker with red illustrated flame tree figures and HELIX text in bold white
description: Helix was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2013 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Cargo Cult theme.

title: BeeCharge Camp
imageAlt: Yellow and black sticker with cartoon bee and bEEcHARGE 7:45ish and C Black Rock City 2012 text
description:
BeeCharge is a San Francisco Bay Area theme camp with a pollinator theme.
Visitors are buzzed into the NectarSector for shade and community. The camp operates two mutant vehicles — the Red Hot Beverly and the Apis — and is recognized as one of Burning Man's clean, sustainable green camps.

title: Camp Scotch & Hop
imageAlt: BM 2025 sticker. Black background with green matrix text. "Tomorrow Today" vertical left. Scotch N' Hop bunny logo. Center Camp Plaza @5:45.
description:
In a world suspended between code and dust, between data and dreams,
our camp—Scotch & Hop—blinks into the present at Center Camp Plaza, 5:45.
A visual glitch in the Matrix, a rabbit wearing goggles, watching the future stream through the now.
The background hums with Burning Man 2025, digital mantra, while 'TOMORROW' looms, and 'TODAY' rises like a command line.
But what about Yesterday?
A whisper beneath the noise.
A question stitched in neon green and memory:
Have we already been here? Yes.

title: Darwin's Monkey Bar
imageAlt: Green circular sticker with cartoon monkey illustration and Camp Above the Law 2001 Darwins Monkey Bar text
description: Darwin's Monkey Bar, another sticker from Camp Above the Limit contributed by Steven Fritz, plays directly on Charles Darwin and Burning Man's 2009 Evolution theme.

title: DMV
imageAlt: White oval sticker with stick figure roadrunner and BRC DMV 2001 text in European car oval style
description: This 2001 sticker represents the Department of Mutant Vehicles (DMV), Burning Man's official program for licensing and regulating the art cars and mutant vehicles allowed on the playa. It was contributed by Steven Fritz during the event's Seven Ages theme year.

title: Bunny Camp
imageAlt: Blue starry background sticker with three cartoon bunny characters in pink jumpsuits and Bunny Camp 2002 text
description:
Bunny Camp is one of Burning Man's long-running theme camps, inviting participants to transcend their humanity and embrace their inner bunny.
Known for plush Esplanade lounges, fur daybeds, craft cocktails, and curated beats at sundown, Bunny Camp has been a BRC fixture since at least 2000.

title: Katlieidoscope
imageAlt: Holographic circular sticker with kaleidoscope Burning Man mandala and zodiac symbols, Burning Man 2023
description:
Designed as a gift by some  people for the people.
The creators: Kat - Katlieidoscope - Gallagher with assistance from Andrew - Master of Ceremonies - McNally

title: Burning Man Documentation Team
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with camera aperture design and Burning Man Documentation Team text arcing around edge
description:
The Burning Man Documentation Team is the official crew of photographers and videographers who capture the event for the archive — the people behind the images that let everyone who was not there imagine what it looked like, and let everyone who was there remember. They operate all week under difficult conditions: dust storms, extreme heat, night shoots, fire, crowds, and the challenge of photographing something that resists easy documentation.
This 2022 sticker is their badge — the Official sticker of the Documentation Team, made for a year that mattered extra because it was the first full-scale return since COVID. Whatever happened in 2022 that was worth remembering, someone from the Doc Team was there to document it.

title: Caravansary - Man and City
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with Burning Man figure in minimalist mandala design and B M letters in geometric layout
description: This sticker was created by Lofax for the 2014 Burning Man event, named directly for that year's Caravansary theme. Beyond the name, year, and creator, no further details are recorded.

title: BM Lady
imageAlt: Circular sticker with intricate colorful mosaic portrait of a woman with decorative patterns in purple and warm tones
description:
When the 2020 Burning Man was canceled due to COVID-19, the Burning Man organization released a free downloadable sketchbook to give the community something creative to do while stuck at home.
This sticker came from that moment — the creator took an image from the official Burning Man sketchbook, originally designed in black and white, and turned it into a full-color sticker.
A piece of participatory culture born from a year when participation had to happen at home. The Playa was virtual. The stickers were real.

title: Soup Ops Sticker
imageAlt: Circular sticker with skull and crossbones in military beret design and Soup Ops text
description: Artist Daniel Kelley’s concept and creation, the Soup Ops Sticker is awarded to Soup Warriors under special circumstances, usually along with a promotion in Rank.

title: Burning Man Project
imageAlt: Round sticker with globe earth image and Making the Planet More Like the Playa Burning Man Project text
description: Burning Man Project is the 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that took over stewardship of the event in 2013, succeeding Black Rock City LLC. This sticker, contributed by Steven Fritz, commemorates that founding year, as the new organization began overseeing Black Rock City and expanding initiatives like Burners Without Borders.

title: Gigsville
imageAlt: White square sticker with Gigsville community description text and tagline Look not everyone from LA is a celebrity
description: This sticker represents Gigsville, a Burning Man theme camp, contributed by Penfold for the 2004 event — the year of the festival's The Vault of Heaven theme.

title: Axis Mundi — Ochre
imageAlt: Circular sticker: an eight-pointed star mandala in reds, blues, greens, purples, ochre border. Text: Burning Man 2026, Axis Mundi, Black Rock City.
description: Clark Stoeckley designed this mandala series for 2026, channeling the Burning Man theme's "cosmic, centering energy" into Islamic geometry-inspired patterns. He gifted 500 sticker packs — these mandalas paired with humorous and political stickers — to burners across Black Rock City, calling the reactions when people opened them one of his favorite moments of the Burn. Stoeckley is a repeat Burning Man muralist (work on the playa in 2009, 2010, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2022, and 2024) and a longtime geometric abstract painter, currently an Associate Professor of Art & Graphic Design at the American University of Kuwait.

title: Not A Cult
imageAlt: Psychedelic sticker: green aliens, rainbow rays, flames. "Not A Cult · Burning Man 2026 · Sobriety & Our Journey to the Playa." Art by @zacharyminnich
description:
Not A Cult is one of Burning Man's most distinctive theme camps — an alcohol-free community dedicated to proving that radical self-expression doesn't need a drink in hand. They host what their bio calls "some of Burning Man's weirdest events" and document the whole journey through the Bigger Life Adventures Podcast. Sober, sincere, and spectacularly weird.
This is their sticker for Burning Man 2026. Designed by @zacharyminnich, it puts the camp's identity front and center — the name, the mission statement, and the address — in the kind of loud, retro-cosmic style that makes it impossible to miss on a water bottle or a van window. Exactly the energy of a camp that's proudly, defiantly themselves.
Going to Burning Man 2026? Find them at B & 3:45 — no password required, no robes, just good people and zero hangovers.

title: Burning Man Mandala
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with intricate wheel mandala design and Burning Man 2004 text around border
description: Burning Man Mandala was created by David Marr for the 2004 event, staged under that year's official theme, The Vault of Heaven — a theme that filled Black Rock City with celestial and cosmic imagery, fitting company for a sticker built around mandala geometry.

title: Holographic Halftone Man
imageAlt: Round holographic sticker with iridescent halftone dot pattern forming a Burning Man figure
description: Holographic Halftone Man was created by Jamen Percy — a longtime Burner known for his aerial photography of Black Rock City, later invited to join Burning Man's official documentation team — and gifted to fellow Burners at the 2018 event, staged under that year's I, Robot theme.

title: Find Your Weird
imageAlt: Colorful illustrated sticker with costumed cartoon figure in playa scene and Find Your Weird Black Rock City text
description: Created by Jean Menezes, this dancing-toad design celebrated the 2023 Burning Man event's official Animalia theme.

title: Cross stitch sticker
imageAlt: Circular cream sticker with cross stitch embroidery style Burning Man figure with planet designs and Burning Man 21 text
description: This cross-stitch design was created by Kat for Left Foot Gang, originally made for the 2020 Burning Man event and then edited and turned into stickers for 2021 — the two years Black Rock City's gathering moved online due to COVID-19, themed Multiverse and The Great Unknown respectively.

title: Animalia - "Official"
imageAlt: Circular Burning Man 2023 “Animalia” gate sticker with vibrant neon animals surrounding stylized text on a dark background.
description:
Every year Burning Man has one official welcome sticker, and this is 2023's version — the one Greeters handed to arriving Burners along with the What, Where, When Guide, Black Rock City's essential survival handbook. 
Illustrated by terratorie for that year's Animalia theme, it works less like sought-after art and more like proof of arrival: everyone who picked up a Guide at the gate got one. 
That makes it one of the most widely distributed pieces in the whole Archive — a small shared memory nearly every 2023 attendee carried out of the gate.

title: Carnival of Mirrors
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with red Burning Man figure and 2015 Carnival of Mirrors text
description: A variant sticker from Burning Man's 2015 art theme 'Carnival of Mirrors,' which explored how modern media and self-image distort reality and perception. The Man stood within a mirrored pavilion and funhouse structure. Multiple sticker editions were produced for this theme.

title: Hot Mess
imageAlt: Holographic pink and blue circular seal sticker with Hot Mess Certified bold text and scalloped border
description: Created by Bextra — who describes herself as "a Certified Hot Mess" — this sticker dates to the 2025 Burning Man event and that year's Tomorrow Today theme.

title: Camp Scotch & Hop
imageAlt: BM 2026 sticker. Ancient oak tree with gnarled roots over a rabbit hole; white rabbit sits at the entrance. Scotch N' Hop bunny logo. Eternal & 8:45.
description:
On the Playa, Scotch N' Hop runs a bar, a lounge, and a bunny shrine — three things you didn't know you needed until you needed them. Named for the spirit and the mascot, they've built a corner of the Playa worth the detour. 
Grab your Scotch & Hop 2026 sticker at their bar, lounge and at the bunny shrine! Follow the rabbit to Eternal & 8:45.

title: Contest Winning Greeter's Sticker
createdBy: Ranger Ralph design in collaboration with Gregg Gordon/Gigart.
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with psychedelic all-seeing eye mandala and Burning Man Metamorphosis 2019 text
description: This was the official, contest-winning Greeter's sticker for the 2019 Burning Man event, designed by Ranger Ralph in collaboration with Gregg Gordon of Gigart. It was distributed by the Greeters, the volunteers who welcome every participant at the gate, during the year of the festival's Metamorphoses theme.

title: Putt-Putt Playa
imageAlt: White oval sticker with PPP Putt Putt Playa Black Rock City NV text in European car sticker style
description: Putt Putt Playa was contributed by Hedy Scerico for the 2008 Burning Man event, held under that year's American Dream theme.

title: Carnival of Mirrors "Official"
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with skeleton figures and rabbit and Burning Man 2015 Carnival of Mirrors text
description: This official sticker was distributed in the "What, Where, When" guide at the 2015 Burning Man event, marking that year's Carnival of Mirrors theme.

title: Hover
imageAlt: Light blue green square sticker with toilet cartoon and If No One Hovers No One Has to Hover Sit the Fuck Down text
description: This Portos camp sticker was created by Cabbage and contributed by Rheanna for the 2022 Burning Man event, held under that year's Waking Dreams theme.

title: Bidet and Night
imageAlt: An illustrated bidet nozzle beside stacked text 'BIDET,' 'AND,' 'NIGHT,' with 'BURNING MAN 2026' below, in white/grey on black.
description: Bidet and Night riffs on 'Night and Day,' swapping in a bidet nozzle for a burst of classic Burning Man bathroom humor — the same irreverent, sanitation-adjacent comedy that runs through PoopClear and plenty of other playa novelty stickers. Homemade wordplay like this is a Black Rock City staple, traded camp to camp long before it ends up in any archive.

title: Animalia Cat
imageAlt: Black-and-white geometric cat face sticker with the words “Burning Man,” “Animalia,” and “2023” around the edges.
description:
Burning Man's 2023 theme, Animalia, asked Black Rock City to see itself as part of the animal kingdom rather than separate from it — animals real and imagined, remembered and mythologized. The theme drew on tonalism, the old belief that every person carries an animal counterpart bound up with who they are, and few animals carry as much of that mythic weight as the cat: worshipped as the goddess Bastet in ancient Egypt, cast as witches' familiars in European folklore, praised by Kipling as the animal that walks by itself. 
Dima contributed this geometric cat-face sticker to the Archive in 2023, a companion piece to their wolf design from the same year.

title: Tree Evolution
imageAlt: White square sticker with botanical DNA tree evolution diagram and EVOLUTION text in minimal style
description: Tree Evolution was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2009 Burning Man event, its name doubling as a direct reference to that year's Evolution theme.

title: Muff Car
imageAlt: Round sticker with illustrated cartoon fox wearing scarf and Muff Car Muff Diver BRC 2021 text
description:
Created this sticker for Ranger Cotton Tail after she loved the idea when it came up during a chat on Burning Man FB page. 
This is the sticker that the operators of the motorized dumpster full of complimentary earmuffs will give to all Burners who take a dive and a ride when they get off. Hasn’t happened yet.

title: This Is Your Brain on Playa
imageAlt: Pink square sticker with cartoon brain wearing sunglasses and Burning Man Black Rock City 1988 text
description: Adam Patch created this sticker to give Black Rock City's citizens a "generic" keepsake not tied to any particular camp or party, dated to the 2018 Burning Man event and that year's I, Robot theme.

title: Burning Man Information Radio
imageAlt: Round white sticker with BRC Metropolis 2010 Welcome Home text and circular radio dial design, BMIR radio
description:
A BMIR camp giveaway from Burning Man 2010, the year of the Metropolis theme. Styled after classic European country-code oval bumper stickers, this black-on-white design arcs Metropolis 2010 above a bold BRC, with Welcome Home! curving below. BMIR printed a fresh version of these ovals each year, changing the theme at the top — making each one a quiet time capsule of the burn it came from.
Simple, iconic, and unmistakably Playa. The BRC oval stickers became one of BMIR's most beloved annual traditions — small gifts passed out at the camp, each one encoding a specific year's theme into a format borrowed from the road signs of another world.

title: Steampunk Saloon
imageAlt: Dark square sticker with skull and crossbones and Blackrock 2013 Steam Punk Saloon text in steampunk style
description: This sticker represents Steampunk Saloon, a Burning Man theme camp from the 2013 event, staged under that year's Cargo Cult theme.

title: No Drama Camp
imageAlt: Oval sticker on black background. White oval reads: "If you bring the drama / No Drama Bar / Burning Man 2018 / You earn the karma".
description:
No Drama Bar has been setting the tone at Black Rock City since 2018 — a camp built around good drinks, daily events, and a strict philosophical door policy. Under a 1,200-square-foot shade structure, they've hosted everything from sunrise happy hours to nightly DJ sets, giving the Playa a place to land when you need the opposite of spectacle.
The motto says it plainly: If you bring the Drama, you earn the Karma. It's a rule that sounds like a joke until you realize they actually mean it — and that's exactly what makes the camp work. No Drama Bar draws the kind of crowd that wants connection over conflict, and sends them back to the Playa a little lighter.

title: Black Rock Center for Unlearning
imageAlt: Dark circular university seal sticker with BRCU 4:00 and Booze Gas text and Fuck What You Know motto
description:
Motto: Fuck what you know. The Black Rock Center for Unlearning was founded in 2009 by a group of mostly first-time burners who found each other in the dust and decided not to leave — at least not spiritually.
About 100 people from around the world now make up this camp family. They run a 24-hour bar, cook two full meals a day for campers (Thursday is Thanksgiving), and bring 4,000 square feet of shade to the Playa.
The curriculum: unlearn everything, then drink about it.

title: Evolution
imageAlt: Dark square sticker with white illustrations of evolution sequence from primate to human and Evolution BRC 2001 text
description: Evolution was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2009 Burning Man event, named directly for that year's official theme.

title: John Frum Search Party
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with Burning Man silhouette and John Frum Search Party Burning Man 2013 text
description:
Sticker by Merv Ellstrom tied to Burning Man's 2013 'Cargo Cult' theme.
John Frum is a mythical figure from Tanna Island, Vanuatu — a WWII American serviceman believed to bring cargo and abundance. Burning Man used the legend to explore technology, communal longing, and systems of belief.

title: Camp Loadie
imageAlt: White circular sticker with cartoon disheveled character and Camp Loadie BRC 2013 text with shamrock
description: This Camp Loadie sticker was gifted to site contributor fingerwave during a visit to see the camp's Landshark art car, dated to the 2013 Burning Man event and that year's Cargo Cult theme.

title: Holographic
imageAlt: Dark rectangular sticker with holographic blue glow, Burning Man figure on playa, and Multiverse 2020 text
description: This 5-by-5-inch holographic sticker was created by Margo for 2020, the year Burning Man's physical event was cancelled due to COVID-19 and replaced with the virtual Multiverse experience.

title: Elektra
imageAlt: Round cream sticker with stylized mermaid fish creature illustration and Elektra text
description: This sticker was created by Engineered Artworks, a California-based art-car and sculpture collective known for large-scale Burning Man builds, for the 2024 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Curiouser & Curiouser theme. Contributor fingerwave recalled watching sunrise from the vehicle.

title: DPW – Fuel Team
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with orange lightning bolt figure in gear cog design and Department of Public Works Fuel Team text
description: DPW Fuel Team refers to the Department of Public Works, the crew responsible for building Black Rock City's infrastructure before Burning Man opens each year. This sticker dates to the 2015 event, held under that year's Carnival of Mirrors theme.

title: Conesexual
imageAlt: Orange-and-white striped pride-flag design with a traffic cone in a heart and the word “Conesexual.”
description: Conesexual is a 2026 Burning Man sticker for Gayte, the theme camp built around gate duty. A tongue-in-cheek pride-flag design by Sparklecorn pairs orange-and-white stripes with a traffic cone inside a heart, standing in for the usual flag symbol.

title: Camp Upsie Dasium
imageAlt: Colorful illustrated sticker with cartoon characters and Camp Upsie Dasium 2013 Black Rock City text
description: This sticker represents Camp Upsie Dasium — also documented under the name Camp GravyBrain — a Burning Man theme camp, contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2013 event, the year of the festival's Cargo Cult theme.

title: BRC Gun and Rowing Club
imageAlt: Light circular sticker with emblem and Black Rock City Gun and Rowing Club Member 2004 text
description:
The BRC Gun and Rowing Club is a classic piece of Burning Man deadpan — a camp name that sounds like it belongs on a plaque outside a Victorian gentlemen's club in London, not in the middle of the Nevada desert during Burning Man 2004's Vault of Heaven theme. The combination of firearms and rowing is precisely the kind of absurd pairing that makes perfect sense at BRC.
Theme camps at Burning Man have always played with institutional identity, setting up mock lodges, clubs, and organizations as a way of lampooning the default world's hierarchies — and inviting strangers to participate in something ridiculous together. The sticker is the membership card.

title: Friendgasm
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with owl face illustration and All Hail the Glory of Rum Ham Friendgasm 2019 text
description: This sticker represents Friendgasm theme camp, contributed by Autum and Scott for the 2019 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Metamorphoses theme. The camp also documented its 2018 Black Rock City experience in a YouTube video.

title: Eggchairsteve
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with orange flames and Burning Man 2003 Black Rock City Beyond Belief text
description:
Stephen 'Eggchair Steve' Bissinger is a Burning Man legend — 24-year veteran, former Design & Graphics lead for the Burning Man organization, and founder of EGGs Bar theme camp.
He began creating annual Burning Man stickers in 1996, making him one of the earliest recurring sticker artists in BRC.

title: Whiskey & Dust Camp
imageAlt: Illustrated sticker with pin-up woman in western hat holding whiskey bottle, Whiskey and Dust Caravansary 2014
description: This Whiskey & Dust Camp sticker is an oil painting on board with digitally added lettering, designed and painted by artist Marie Vlasic. Whiskey & Dust is a Colorado-based theme camp centered on whiskey education and yoga, established in 2009. This sticker is dated to the 2014 Burning Man event and that year's Caravansary theme.

title: Da Vinci inspired
imageAlt: Sepia tone sticker with Da Vinci-style technical drawing of Burning Man figure with measurements, ESD 2016
description: ESD 2016 was created by Lofax for the 2016 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Da Vinci's Workshop theme.

title: More Carrot
imageAlt: Yellow diamond road sign style sticker with two stick figures and More Carrot text
description:
More Carrot is a Burning Man theme camp built around the guiding philosophy of "more carrot, less stick" — rewarding effort and generosity rather than policing behavior. Emerging out of Burning Man 2008-2009, the international collective of artists, musicians, and volunteers became known for running a playa farmer's market, handing out fresh produce and smoothies to passersby.
This sticker, contributed by Steven Fritz, marks the camp's presence at the 2009 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Evolution theme.

title: Temple of the Stars
imageAlt: Dark blue circular sticker with illuminated Temple of Stars architectural illustration in gold and teal tones
description: The Temple of Stars was the official 2004 Temple at Burning Man, designed and built by David Best, continuing the annual Temple tradition he helped establish in 2000 with the very first Temple, the Temple of the Mind. It was built during the year of the festival's The Vault of Heaven theme.

title: Taco Disco
imageAlt: Dark square sticker with disco ball and taco illustration and Taco Disco bold text
description: "Imagine seeing the taco of your munchy dreams floating across your view, dispensing great tunes and vibes whenever it is stopped, bringing joy to all." - Taco Disco.

title: Animalia
imageAlt: White square sticker with geometric faceted animal face in black linework and 2023 text
description:
The 2023 Burning Man theme was ANIMALIA — a full celebration of the animal world in all its forms.
This community-submitted design works in the white spectrum: pale creatures, light forms, the quieter side of the animal kingdom rendered in sticker form.
At Burning Man, the animal costumes come out in force — and this sticker belongs to that tradition.

title: Life is Very Good Here
imageAlt: Cream circular sticker with hand-drawn minimalist tree illustration and Life is Very Good Here text
description: Life Is Very Good Here dates to the 2005 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Psyche theme. The sticker's creator isn't recorded beyond the name and year.

title: The Gated Community EST. 1986
imageAlt: Pentagon-shaped sticker showing two uniformed guards at a fence, with hand holding tickets and text “The Gated Community Est. 1986".
description: This sticker, "The Gated Community EST. 1986," was submitted by Dima for the 2025 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Tomorrow Today theme. Specific design details haven't been documented yet.

title: Camp Balls Soup Can
imageAlt: Photorealistic red and white soup can with Camp Balls Condensed Checkin Noods Moop label
description: Camp Balls Soup Can was the first sticker Scott made for Camp Balls. Early feedback encouraging him to "expand it" led to the design becoming the camp's patch as well. It's dated to the 2020 Burning Man event, the year Black Rock City's in-person gathering was replaced by the virtual Multiverse event due to COVID-19.

title: Larry Harvey & Metropolis
imageAlt: Colorful illustrated sticker with portrait of Larry Harvey and Metropolis Burning Man artwork
description:
Tribute to Burning Man co-founder Larry Harvey, created for the 2010 Metropolis theme.
Harvey conceived Burning Man on a San Francisco beach in 1986 and developed its guiding 10 Principles. He served as Executive Director until his passing in April 2018.

title: Cotton Candy Camp
imageAlt: Simple illustrated robot with pom-poms and one eye, with text “Burning Man 2018,” “I Robot,” and “Cotton Candy Camp, 6:00 & E.”
description: This sticker represents Cotton Candy Camp, submitted by Dima, dated to the 2018 Burning Man event and that year's I, Robot theme. Specific design details haven't been documented yet.

title: occult? a cult...
imageAlt: Bronze coin-style circular sticker with Im in a Cult text and Burning Man figure design
description: This death b4 decaf camp sticker was created by simon of the playa for the 2022 Burning Man event, with the tagline "don't join us, we'll join you." It arrived during the year of the festival's Waking Dreams theme.

title: Burner City
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with concentric city rings, central flame symbol, and BURNER 2006 text
description:
Burning Man 2006's theme was Hope and Fear: The Future — a meditation on what comes next, on the cities we build and what we hope they'll become. Burner City lands squarely in that conversation. A city of burners. A city that is only temporary, only real for one week, and yet somehow more fully realized as a community than most permanent cities ever manage.
The name functions as both a description and a claim: this is a city, and its citizens are burners. It is equal parts affectionate and declarative. The sticker is a document of belonging — proof that you are from somewhere, even if that somewhere disappears every September.

title: Safety Third
imageAlt: Yellow diamond road sign sticker with stick figure and Safety Thrid text, deliberate misspelling parody
description: Safety Third was created by Jamen Percy — a longtime Burner and aerial photographer later invited onto Burning Man's official documentation team — and gifted to fellow Burners at the 2018 event, staged under that year's I, Robot theme, as a playful twist on the standard "safety first" refrain.

title: Green Man
imageAlt: White oval sticker with green BRC text, Green Man silhouette, and Crew the Man text
description:
The Green Man was Burning Man's 2007 art theme, exploring humanity's relationship to nature.
It marked the event's first major environmental initiative: generators ran on biodiesel and the Man Pavilion ran on solar. A ring of trees made from recycled industrial materials — the Mangrove — circled the Man.

title: Cameltopia
imageAlt: Retro banner sticker: camel, pyramids, palm trees. Gold text on teal: "Cameltopia · Since 2014 · 3:45 & Fascinate." Vintage travel poster style.
description:
Cameltopia has been a fixture since 2014 — a desert oasis where Burners rehydrate, browse the Inconvenience Store, and make it to Wednesday's legendary Hump Day party. Part post-apocalyptic Route 66 gas station, part community watering hole, it's one of Black Rock City's most enduring theme camps.
This is their 2024 sticker, designed by Clark (aka This Motherfucker) — a retro travel banner that wears the camp's twelve years of Playa history like a badge. The kind of sticker you put on a water bottle and people ask about every time.

title: Opposable Thumbs
imageAlt: Dark red square sticker with thumbs up cartoon and Opposable Thumbs Evolution Rocks Burning Man 2009 text
description: Opposable Thumbs was contributed by Tim Schapker for the 2009 Burning Man event, playing on that year's Evolution theme — opposable thumbs being one of the textbook markers of human evolutionary development.

title: Tomorrow Today
imageAlt: Purple sticker with neon pink Burning Man figure with lightning bolts and Burning Man 2022 text
description: Tomorrow Today was created by Rory Kalmar as a personal swag item for the 2025 Burning Man event, named directly for that year's official theme.

title: Matter Out Of Place
imageAlt: Square sticker with sci-fi circular graphics and the text “MOOP – Matter Out Of Place” and “Get that shit out of here” on a dark textured background.
description: I don't know anything about this sticker. If you do, please use the Contact form (opens in a new tab) to let me know so I can update it here. Thanks, fingerwave

title: Camp Balls – Soup Can Label
imageAlt: Photorealistic soup can label in Campbell style with Camp Balls Soup Checkin Noods text
description: This Camp Balls sticker, created by Scott, was designed as a soup-can-style label for 2021 — the year Burning Man's in-person gathering was again called off for COVID-19, with participants organizing independent regional gatherings instead of the official event.

title: Flaming Lotus Girls - NOETICA
imageAlt: Dark square sticker with black and white checkerboard pattern and Burning Man 2017 Flaming Lotus Girls Noetica text
description: Noetica was Flaming Lotus Girls' 2017 Burning Man Honorarium piece, contributed by Gregg Adams — two sculptures built from 144 stainless steel squares each, with the larger hydraulically controlled by the smaller. It was built during the year of the festival's Radical Ritual theme.

title: The Future
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with red triskelion triple spiral symbol and BM 2006 The Future text on black background
description: The Future was contributed by Raffi for the 2006 Burning Man event, directly evoking that year's Hope and Fear theme.

title: Cat & Butterfly
imageAlt: Holographic sticker of a detailed cat face topped with colorful butterfly wings and geometric patterns, with “2023” near the top.
description: This sticker was submitted by Dima for the 2023 Burning Man event — the year of the festival's Animalia theme, fittingly matched to its cat-and-butterfly imagery. Further design details haven't been documented yet.

title: Woonanmi Village
imageAlt: Dark red sticker with decorative bug and spider creature illustrations and Woonamaste Woonami Village 2003 text
description: This sticker represents Woonanmi Village, a Burning Man theme camp contributed by Tanya Zumach, continuing from the camp's 2002 sticker (recorded on this site as Woonami Village) into the 2003 event — the year of the festival's Beyond Belief theme.

title: Taco Disco
imageAlt: Taco Disco sticker: a taco-shaped art car with LED lights and a disco ball, from Burning Man 2026.
description:
Taco Disco is a mobile art car built by Wildstone Arts on a 2008 Mini Truck base, topped with a giant taco structure wrapped in 400 watts of programmable LEDs and floodlights. A disco-ball simulator turns the ground beside it into an instant dance floor, backed by a DJ table, 2,600 watts of onboard sound, and flame effects up front.
True to its name, the crew doubles as a mobile taqueria, serving hot tacos alongside the music out in the deep playa. This sticker marks Taco Disco's presence at the 2026 Burning Man event, staged under that year's official Axis Mundi theme.

title: Camp FUCK
imageAlt: Green square sticker with FUCK text repeated in grid and Burning Man figures in colorful punk style
description: Camp Fuck's sticker was contributed by Patrick Rose for the 2005 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Psyche theme. No further details about the piece's design or origin are recorded.

title: Don't just exist LIVE!
imageAlt: Black sticker with text “Don’t just exist… LIVE!” and a stylized figure between two campfires.
description: This sticker, "Don't Just Exist LIVE!", was submitted by Dima for the 2025 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Tomorrow Today theme. Specific design details haven't been documented yet.

title: Perpetual Evolution
imageAlt: Gray circular clock gauge sticker with Burning Man figure and minimal clock face design
description: Perpetual Evolution was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2009 Burning Man event, directly referencing that year's official theme.

title: Evolve
imageAlt: Yellow square sticker with primate to human evolution silhouette sequence and Evolve Burning Man 2009 Evolution text
description: Evolve I was contributed by squishelle for the 2009 Burning Man event, drawing its name straight from that year's Evolution theme.

title: FOMO
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with large red FOMO text in prohibition crossed circle design with fire background
description: FOMO — Fear of Missing Out — was created by squishelle for the 2015 Burning Man event, with 1,000 copies printed, during that year's Carnival of Mirrors theme.

title: Feminine Power Collective
imageAlt: Dark badge sticker with hands embrace design and Feminine Power Collective Burning Woman Plan B text
description: Feminine Power Collective is a 3″ Glitter Card, part of the Camp Balls Glitter Card 2021 series. To the best of my knowledge, there is no Feminine Power Collective although the idea seemed to have appeal.

title: Playa Magic 2026
imageAlt: Square sticker with the words "Playa Magic" in yellow on a grey background.
description: "This is the first ever sticker for Playa Magic! 2026 is our first year. I founded Playa Magic to embody the thing that keeps people coming back year after year: the concept of 'Playa magic'. For our interactivity we bring Burning Man’s first ever civic lottery to the Playa: the BRC Lottery Commission!" — Lord Kai.

title: I’m kind of a big deal at Burning Man
imageAlt: Purple rectangular sticker with large black Im Kind of a Big Deal at Burning Man text and Burning Man figure 2017
description: This sticker, contributed by Ed, was gifted to Scrubby's Angels, crew of the Scrubby Bubble mutant vehicle — a 1950s mini fire truck built by Eddy Bullock in Detroit and known as one of Black Rock City's cleanest-looking art cars. It's dated to the 2017 Burning Man event and that year's Radical Ritual theme.

title: Camp Fuck Yeah
imageAlt: Dark sticker with illustrated group of demonic creature characters and The Orphans Fuck Yeah text
description:
After almost two decades, Camp Fuck Yeah collapsed in July ‘24. The remaining human fragments can still be seen everywhere around the Burn, drifting in the dust. 
The evolution, memories and legacy of our camp will never be replaced. We still remain connected as clusters of humans, The Orphans of Fuck Yeah. A big spiderweb of family bonded for life

title: The Great Unknown
imageAlt: Dark square sticker with colorful psychedelic holographic geometric spheres and circles
description: The Great Unknown, created by Bread, takes its name from Burning Man's official 2021 theme. It was built from what the creator described as "the BORG graphic."

title: American Dream
imageAlt: White circular sticker with Burning Man figure in American flag design and American Dream II Burning Man 2004 text
description:
Sticker from Burning Man's 2008 'American Dream' theme — the first explicitly political theme since 1996.
The Man stood atop a 60-foot obelisk flying flags of all nations except the United States. Over 240 art projects explored patriotism, immigration, and the mythology of the American dream.

title: Gary I Robot
imageAlt: Colorful psychedelic circular sticker with cartoon robot character in cosmic setting and Art text, Gary iRobot theme
description:
It is good to know that when not at Black Rock City, CampCampCampers live on Planet awesome.
Rather than having to deal with exodus and long lines of cars, they simply hop on and off Playa via the pyramid portal at the center of the theme camp. The best way of transport is usually found on a miniature sized spoon.

title: Leave No Trace
imageAlt: Dark blue square sticker with globe earth illustration and Leave No Trace bold text
description: This sticker was created in parody of the logo of the Sherman Williams “Cover the Earth” logo with the alternate “Leave No Trace.” Handed out 1,000 of these at the 2019 Burn from the Lamplighters camp.

title: Matcho Sticker
imageAlt: Circular sticker with cartoon luchador wrestler figure and Up Bomb Black Rock City text
description:
This Lip Bomb camp sticker was created by Mark Matcho, a Los Angeles-based illustrator whose bold, concept-driven artwork has appeared in The New York Times, Rolling Stone, and Time, among other major publications, over a three-decade career.
Contributed by Scott Mertz for the 2017 Burning Man event — called at the time "a very cool project" — it arrived during the year of the festival's Radical Ritual theme.

title: Animalia Wings
imageAlt: Holographic sticker showing two mirrored animal faces with a rainbow light streak and small text reading “Burning Man” and “Animalia.”
description:
Wings mean something different at Burning Man than anywhere else.
The Playa has a way of making flight feel possible — not metaphorically but viscerally. This sticker from the 2023 ANIMALIA theme captures that: wings rendered for a city where people routinely build the things they dream about and then wear them into the desert.

title: Metropolis
imageAlt: Dark sticker with Chicago skyline at night, glowing blue Burning Man figure, and Burning Man 2010 Metropolis text
description: Metropolis 2010 was created by Ben Pearson and gifted to fellow Burners at the 2010 Burning Man event, named directly for that year's official theme.

title: The Free Love Bird View Man
imageAlt: Square sticker with colorful abstract design and The Free Love Bird View Man Burning Man 2023 text
description:
The matching sticker to THE FREE LOVE BIRD VIEW MAN, 2022 Rhinestone Pendant by Sophie Graubner from Germany.
The stunning production pendant with 57 Rhinestones is modeled after the 18k solid Gold version with 105 colored Sapphire Gemstones.
Sophie said “I designed it and found a master jeweler who then custom made if for me with Sapphires and set in 18k Gold.
I put the rainbow colored stones the the arms and legs of the man, it’s standing for FREE LOVE, so everybody should love whoever every person wants to and I thinks it’s unbelievable and not correct that many people were told to marry people they don’t know (arranged marriages) in the 2020s.
And I put this together with the bird view: I put the open circle which is Black Rock City from the BIRD VIEW and the stones in the head of the man have special positions from the bird view and linked to the open circle:
The big blue stone is the position of THE MAN and blue was the favorite color of Burning Man founder Larry Harvey
The green stone is the position of the temple and green is the color for good hope
 The little stones stand for the different art sculptures which stand in the Playa.“

title: Sparkle Stallion
imageAlt: Round sticker with pastel playa landscape and cartoon pony character, Sparkle Stallion 2020 text
description: “Scott Whitaker helped me to digitize this design. It’s an inside joke with one of my friends, instead of just a sparkle pony, he aspires to be a sparkle stallion. The “stallion” is shirt cocking against the backdrop of the Black Rock Desert” – Kelly.

title: Burning Man Tried To Kill Me
imageAlt: Black rectangular sticker with white text reading “Burning Man tried to kill me.”
description: This sticker was submitted by Dima for the 2025 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Tomorrow Today theme. Specific design details haven't been documented yet.

title: White Rabbit
imageAlt: Dark sticker with portrait of anthropomorphic white rabbit in top hat and glasses, Curious and Curiouser Black Rock City text
description: "I designed this myself for this years theme. Inspired by the Alice in Wonderland's White Rabbit and my Theme Camp friends at red nose district. Made as a gift to give to anyone" - Laura.

title: Black Rock Solar
imageAlt: Black Rock Solar sticker. "Free the Sun." Green sunburst over mountain silhouette. Burning Man nonprofit, 2009.
description:
Black Rock Solar started in 2007 as a volunteer crew installing a 30-kilowatt solar array at Burning Man. It turned into something much larger.
The organization went on to install 7.6 megawatts of solar across Nevada — powering schools, tribal colleges, Native American cultural centers, and communities that needed clean affordable energy most. In 2017 it transitioned into Black Rock Labs, a clean-tech accelerator.
What began as a camp project became a genuine solar nonprofit, born from the Playa.

title: Big Puffy Yellow
imageAlt: Yellow sticker with cartoon yellow blob character, Big Puffy Yellow 2013 text, and It Aint Gonna Puff Itself tagline
description:
Founded in 2001 by burners from Charlotte, NC, Big Puffy Yellow has spent over two decades spreading shenanigans, tomfoolery, ballyhoo, and very good house music across Black Rock City.
The original crew is now scattered from NYC to LA to New Orleans to London, but the camp holds together every summer — a yellow-themed gathering of people who know how to have exactly the right amount of fun. They also show up at Transformus and Love Burn.
The sticker is as recognizable as the camp.

title: Cargo Cult
imageAlt: Round sticker with crossed sticks cargo cult design and Burning Man 2013 Cargo Cult The Playa Nevada text
description: Cargo Cult was created by Merv Ellstrom and contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2013 Burning Man event, named directly for that year's official theme — inspired by the real historical phenomenon in which some Pacific Island communities built ritual imitations of Western cargo infrastructure after World War II, hoping to summon the material abundance that had arrived with soldiers.

title: Drink Water
imageAlt: Round teal sticker with cartoon frog and Drink Water Neptune for Mayor Black Rock City Carnival of Mirrors text
description: Drink Water was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2006 Burning Man event, noted at the time with the tagline "Neptune for Mayor." It arrived during the year of the festival's Hope and Fear theme.

title: Man Timeline
imageAlt: Horizontal green pixel art strip sticker showing Burning Man effigy designs across multiple years as a timeline
description: Man Timeline was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2012 Burning Man event, the year of the festival's Fertility 2.0 theme.

title: Eggchairsteve
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with ornate gold ring border and Burning Man 2000 Black Rock City text
description: This sticker is part of Stephen Bissinger's long-running "Eggchairsteve" series, contributed for the 2000 Burning Man event at Black Rock City. That year's official theme was The Body, reflected across the event in everything from art placement to street names drawn from anatomy.

title: The Green Man
imageAlt: Illustrated sticker with tree and human figure in warm earth tones and Burning Man Green Man theme
description: The Green Man sticker, contributed by Ursula Sadiq, takes its name directly from Burning Man's 2007 theme of the same name. It was distributed alongside that year's What Where When guide, the event's official map and schedule booklet.

title: Black Rock French Quarter
imageAlt: Dark rectangular sticker with neon blue Black Rock City text and asterisk crosshairs symbol
description:
The Black Rock French Quarter sticker is a masterpiece of Playa parody: a spoof of the iconic Patagonia logo, but where the mountain range would normally be you get Black Rock City's own landmarks — Center Camp, the Spires, the Man.
It is the kind of visual joke that rewards people who know both references, and it pays off completely.
The camp itself brings New Orleans energy to the Nevada desert during Burning Man, channeling the French Quarter's anything-goes spirit into the anything-goes city.

title: Multiverse
imageAlt: Circular Burning Man sticker labeled “Multiverse 2020,” featuring the Man symbol over a dark geometric pattern with multicolored reflective accents.
description: This silver Multiverse sticker was submitted by Dima for the 2020 Burning Man event — the year Black Rock City's in-person gathering was replaced by the virtual Multiverse event due to COVID-19. Specific design details haven't been documented yet.

title: Flaming Lotus Girls
imageAlt: Dark diamond sticker with white line drawing of flame lotus design and Flaming Lotus Girls text
description: A third entry in the 2010 Flaming Lotus Girls series contributed by Steven Fritz, again from that year's Metropolis-themed Burning Man event.

title: 5 star
imageAlt: Dark sticker with five star rating and Burning Man 2020 The Multiverse Fucked Would Not Recommend parody review
description:
Burning Man had never canceled Black Rock City before 2020 — then COVID-19 made the call unavoidable. On April 10, 2020, organizers scrapped the in-person event but refused to drop that year's already-chosen theme, The Multiverse, instead leaning into it for a ticketed online gathering they called Virtual Black Rock City. 
For a community built on showing up in the dust together, burning from home stung — and gallows humor became how a lot of Burners got through it. Erin's sticker captures that moment: equal parts grief and punchline, gifted to The Archive as a record of the strangest year Black Rock City never happened.

description: This Metamorphoses-themed sticker was created by Eric Cifani, based on a 2011 photograph of the Man by George Post, a longtime Burning Man photographer whose work has been widely published and exhibited. It marks the 2019 event and its official Metamorphoses theme.

description: Flying Pig was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2012 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Fertility 2.0 theme.

description: Created by Shannon Nehls (La Gata Rosa) for Camp Exclamation Mark, this design began as a sticker-contest collaboration and was also adapted into a flyer for the camp's Ten Principles Zoom discussion. It's dated to the 2022 Burning Man event and that year's Waking Dreams theme.

description: This Heart BRC sticker is dated to the 2010 Burning Man event, held under that year's Metropolis theme. Its designer isn't currently known — the site's contributors have noted it predates their own involvement.

description: "I Made It To Medical" is a survivor-badge design for the 2026 Burning Man event, playing on BM Medical — the Black Rock City Emergency Services Department's real on-site medical branch, which treats participants through fixed stations, mobile response units, and the MASH-style Rampart field hospital. No creator or camp is currently documented for this sticker.

imageAlt: Red nametag sticker with Hello My Name Is format and Burner written in blue and Burning Man 2011 Rites of Passage text

imageAlt: Black sticker with red abstract tribal creature design and Woonami Village Black Rock City 2002 text
description: This sticker represents Woonami Village, a Burning Man theme camp, contributed by Tanya Zumach for the 2002 event — the year of the festival's The Floating World theme. No further details about the camp's specific activities that year are recorded.

title: Hello My Playa Name Is (blue)
imageAlt: Blue rectangular nametag sticker with Hello My Playa Name Is text and blank white fill-in area
description: This blue variant of "Hello, My Playa Name Is," created by Clark / This Motherfucker, debuted at the 2023 Burning Man event and has been reprinted and given out every year since — playing on the tradition of Burners adopting a "playa name" for the event.

title: Dick Heads
imageAlt: White vertical sticker with Metropolis BRC 2010 Dick Heads text in bold black
description: Dick Heads was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2010 Burning Man event, the year of the festival's Metropolis theme.

title: Temple of Atonement
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with red Burning Man figure and Temple of Atonement Repent Sin text repeated in arc
description: Temple of Atonement was contributed by Rick Hindman for the 2003 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Beyond Belief theme. It's a separate piece from that year's official Temple, the Temple of Honor — beyond the name, year, and contributor, no further details are recorded.

title: Burners Unite
imageAlt: White circular sticker with two linked figures above flames and Burners Unite text
description:
This sticker was made for a Facebook group gift exchange called Can't Find My Way Home — a swag swap event organized by burners for burners during the years when Burning Man was canceled or limited by COVID. The group name says it all: we are people who belong somewhere, and that somewhere is currently closed.
Burners Unite is a rallying sticker born from absence. It is the kind of thing you make when you cannot go to the place but you still need to connect with the people. A small piece of community infrastructure — the gift economy operating through the mail, across a pandemic, between people who have never met in person but share a city they both call home.

title: There Will Be Dust
imageAlt: Gray square sticker with There Will Be Dust text over playa landscape photograph
description: There Will Be Dust was created by Steven for the 2013 Burning Man event, held under that year's Cargo Cult theme.

title: Bunny Camp
imageAlt: Colorful illustrated sticker with anime-style rabbit characters and Bunny Camp 2003 text on patterned background
description:
2003 was Burning Man's Beyond Belief year — a theme about spirituality, faith, and the sacred spaces we create together. Bunny Camp was there for it, producing their third sticker in four years. By this point the camp had established itself as a returning presence on the Playa, with a recognizable identity and a loyal following.
Three stickers across four years (2000, 2001, 2003) is a quiet kind of commitment. It means the camp kept coming back, kept making something to hand out, kept being a place people wanted to find. The 2003 sticker is the last in the series the catalog holds — and every series has to end somewhere.

title: Camp Upsie Dasium
imageAlt: Hot pink rectangular sticker with Burning Man stick figure and Todays Forecast Fucked Camp Upsie Daisium BRC 2014 text
description: Another Camp Upsie Dasium — also known as Camp GravyBrain — sticker, created by Captain Danger, this one dated to the 2014 Burning Man event, the year of the festival's Caravansary theme, and marked at the time with the tagline "Today's Forecast: Fucked."

title: Emergency Services Department
themeCampName: Lakes of Fire - Emergency Services Department
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with gold caduceus and flame design and Emergency Services Department Lakes of Fire text
description: This patch was made by the Lakes of Fire Swag team for the event's Emergency Services Department. Lakes of Fire is the Great Lakes region's official Burning Man regional event, held annually in Rothbury, Michigan. It was contributed by Joel Eastlund and dated to 2024.

title: Gypsy “Renegade” Kitties Theme Camp
imageAlt: Circular sticker with illustrated cat wearing sunglasses and Renegade Kitties Speakeasy text
description: Another Gypsy Kitties camp sticker, created by fingerwave and gifted at the 2016 Burning Man event, held under that year's Da Vinci's Workshop theme.

title: You’re Doing It Wrong
imageAlt: Orange and black square sticker with bold Youre Doing It Wrong text
description: "You're Doing It Wrong" is the companion sticker to "You're Doing It Right," both created by Clark / This Motherfucker and reprinted and given out every year since their 2023 Burning Man debut.

title: American Dream - The Man
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with metallic American Dream arc text, Burning Man figure, and 08 Burning Man text
description:
Burning Man's 2008 theme, The American Dream, was the event's first explicitly political theme since 1996 — asking the nearly 50,000 participants in Black Rock City to weigh what America had achieved against what left them uneasy, without picking a side. 
That year's Man stood atop a 66-foot obelisk ringed with the flags of every nation except the United States, a choice Burners still debate. 
Who made this particular American Dream sticker has been lost to time — like plenty of pieces from the Archive's earliest years, it survives without a name attached, one more artifact from a theme that asked Black Rock City to hold up a mirror to the country itself.

title: Whiskey & Dust Camp
imageAlt: Circular sticker with illustrated woman with purple hair holding whiskey bottle, Whiskey and Dust Camp 2016 text
description: This Whiskey & Dust Camp sticker is an oil painting on board with digitally added lettering, designed and painted by artist Marie Vlasic. Whiskey & Dust is a Colorado-based theme camp centered on whiskey education and yoga, established in 2009. This sticker is dated to the 2016 Burning Man event and that year's Da Vinci's Workshop theme.

title: City Of Black Rock
imageAlt: Dark circular coin sticker with City of Black Rock Burning Man MMXC text and geometric crosshair design
description: City of Black Rock dates to the 2010 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Metropolis theme. Beyond the name and year, no further details about this sticker's design or origin are recorded.

title: Carousel Numinous
imageAlt: Cream sticker with hand-drawn religious symbols including cross Star of David skull and eye, Carousel Numinous Black Rock City 2003 text
description: Carousel Numinous was an art project created by John Mosbaugh and Jenny Bird for the 2003 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Beyond Belief theme — an invitation for artists to build works evoking spiritual and visionary experience, fitting territory for a piece whose name points directly to the numinous, a sense of divine or awe-inspiring presence.

title: Greening the Burn
imageAlt: Green circular sticker with stylized plant leaf illustration and Greening the Burn Reduce Reuse Recycle text
description: Before the 2006 event, members of the Greening Man group collectively designed a logo, which was turned into a limited production sticker to hand out at the event.

title: L2K

description:
The sticker for Tim Black's installation of synchronized lights around the man, the L2K ring. _wizard@mad-scientists.com
L2k, the ring of lights around the Man, has been around for several years. In 2001, it became one of Burning Man’s officially funded art projects.
"We cannot stressed enough that driving over the ring does damage it" - Tim Kendziorsk (Manager of L2K)

Well, this year was before the "metamorphosis" theme year.  So I thought I was being clever using a metamorphosis of caterpillar -> cocoon to Man-Butterfly as an example of a rite of passage. - Halcyon.
Not sure if the "caterpillar-as-lamplighter" is clear, but that was the idea. 😛 - Halcyon.

description: Momi Fire was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2012 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Fertility 2.0 theme.
