description: This original design by Dima directly names the 2025 Burning Man event's official Tomorrow Today theme.

title: Camp Hazard
imageAlt: Dark square sticker with orange fire illustration and Burn 2001 Caravansary text
description: Camp Hazard's 2001 sticker was made by Pater and Stephan for that year's Black Rock City. Burning Man's official theme in 2001 was Seven Ages, an event-long allegory that cast the playa as a giant board game carrying participants through the stages of a life — Cradle, Playground, Chapel, Coliseum, Temple of Wisdom, Maze, and Mausoleum.

title: Holographic Man
imageAlt: Round holographic sticker with iridescent rainbow mandala and Burning Man figure
description: Created by Eric, this design was printed as a 3-inch holographic sticker for the 2020 Burning Man event and later adapted into UV-reactive pendants, pins, large weatherproof stickers, and patches. 2020 was the year Black Rock City's in-person gathering was replaced by the virtual Multiverse event due to COVID-19.

title: Guardians
imageAlt: Circular sticker: two torch-bearing guardian figures flank a glowing geodesic dome under flames and stars. Text: Orgy Dome Guardians, 2026.
description: Every year, someone wanders the playa looking for the Orgy Dome and ends up nowhere close. That mix-up inspired this piece from Java and Kristin: a nod to the volunteers who keep watch over Black Rock City's best-known consent-based intimacy space, minding it without ever crowding it — "great pushes from a small distance," as their own motto puts it.

title: Caravansary "Official" BRC Sticker

description: This was the official Black Rock City sticker for the 2014 Burning Man event, made for that year's Caravansary theme. Its minimalist design shows just the Man's head and arms; the designer isn't currently known.

title: DMV Hotties
imageAlt: Dark sticker with line art running figure and Department of Mutant Vehicles Burning Man 2004 DMV Hotties text
description: This sticker represents the Department of Mutant Vehicles (DMV), Burning Man's official program for licensing and regulating the art cars and mutant vehicles permitted on the playa, from the 2004 event held under that year's The Vault of Heaven theme.

title: Bliss Beau
imageAlt: Dark sticker with BRC 2012 text, cartoon pink elephant, and Bliss Beau camp name in colorful tropical design
description:
Beau Le'Phant is a giant pink elephant mutant vehicle built by Dr. Galaxo Magic and the GravyBrain crew.
Its skeleton is PVC pipe covered in pink ripstop nylon, lit from within, rolling on the chassis of a 1989 Chevy C20 van. The vehicle appeared on the Playa in 2011 and returned in 2012 — both times funded in part through Kickstarter.
Large enough to be unmissable, pink enough to be surreal, gentle enough to be beloved. On a dark Playa night, a glowing pink elephant is exactly what you need to see.

title: Flaming Lotus Girls
imageAlt: Blue diamond shaped sticker with Flaming Lotus Girls fire flower logo
description: This sticker, contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2009 Burning Man event, represents Flaming Lotus Girls, the all-women fire arts collective known for large-scale sculptures at Black Rock City across many years. It arrived during the year of the festival's Evolution theme.

title: Mayan Warrior
imageAlt: White circular sticker with minimal MW monogram and Mayan Warrior text in minimalist style
description:
This is a beautiful shiny silver sticker. Unfortunately it did not show up when photographed.
"This sticker was gifted to me in 2016 when I was fortunate enough to be invited on to the Mayan Warrior Art Car.
So far my most memorable sunrise" - fingerwave.

title: Rites of Passage
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with fire phoenix design and Burning Man 2011 Rites of Passage text
description: Rites of Passage was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2011 Burning Man event, named directly for that year's official theme — an event-long meditation on the ceremonies that mark life's major transitions.

title: Metropolis
imageAlt: Black and white square sticker with stylized dancer figure silhouette and Metropolis Burning Man 10 text
description: This unofficial Metropolis sticker was created by Sticky for the 2010 Burning Man event, depicting the Man amid imagery evoking "the diminishment of the worker" — a nod to that year's official Metropolis theme.

title: Burners on Board
imageAlt: Burners On Board
description:
A plural update to the classic Burner on Board concept — now there are more of you. Burners on Board is a car window sticker for the vehicle carrying multiple members of the culture back into the default world after the burn. The 2019 Burning Man theme was Metamorphoses, and the drive home after a week on the Playa is one of the more disorienting metamorphoses most burners experience.
There is something specific about driving through the Nevada desert after Burning Man — dusty, probably exhausted, probably changed — and knowing everyone in the car went through it with you. This sticker communicates that to everyone else on the highway: this car carries people who just came from somewhere you probably have not been.

title: Metropolis
imageAlt: Wide rectangular sticker with aerial panoramic view of art installation and Burning Man Metropolis 2010 text
description: Metropolis Theme 2010, contributed by Steven Fritz, rounds out this site's set of stickers referencing Burning Man's 2010 Metropolis theme.

imageAlt: Dark square sticker with crow in woodcut style and Burning Man 2014 Caravansary Black Rock City Nevada text
description: This sticker was created by Merv Ellstrom and contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2014 Burning Man event, named for that year's official theme, Caravansary.

title: Sunrise Mimosas
imageAlt: Sticker reading “Sunrise Mimosas” with neon-style sun graphic; playful reference to post-party sunrise drinks at Burning Man camps.
description: "This is the sticker for my art project: serving Mimosas at sunrise by the man's embers on Sunday. Not to be confused with the Mimosa Sunrise theme camp!" - Airbender

title: Our City
imageAlt: Circular red-and-green sticker with black radial grid resembling the Burning Man city layout viewed from above.
description: This sticker, "Our City," was submitted by Dima for the 2025 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Tomorrow Today theme. Specific design details haven't been documented yet.

title: Camp Above The Limit
imageAlt: Dark rectangular sticker with silhouetted figures and Camp Above the Limit 2008 text on horizontal band
description: Camp Above the Limit's 2009 sticker played on that year's Evolution theme with the tagline "Beervolution: Survival of the Hoppiest," contributed by Steven Fritz.

title: BRC Kampgrounds
imageAlt: Bold sticker with large red X shape and BRC Kampgrounds text on yellow-orange background
description:
KOA Kampgrounds — America's most recognizable chain of roadside camping — has a very specific visual identity: the logo, the yellow wagons, the cheerful K where a C should be. BRC Kampgrounds takes that branding and drops it into the most unconventional temporary city on earth. The joke lands hard if you know KOA, and it lands even harder if you've ever pulled into Black Rock City and thought: this is nothing like any campground I have ever visited.
Burning Man 2004's theme was Vault of Heaven. Celestial, cosmic, infinite. And somewhere in that vast temporary city, someone set up a Kampground. The sticker exists as evidence.

title: Eggchairsteve
imageAlt: Orange circular sticker with sunburst radiating design and Burning Man 2002 Black Rock City text
description: The 2002 installment of Stephen Bissinger's annual "Eggchairsteve" sticker series, made for that year's Burning Man event. The 2002 theme, The Floating World, filled Black Rock City with a nautical motif, from the Man himself perched atop an 80-foot lighthouse to mutant vehicles built as ships and sea creatures.

title: Conscious
imageAlt: Holographic iridescent sticker with Burning Man 2005 The Pancho text and robot figure
description: Conscious was contributed by Snuggles for the 2005 Burning Man event, fittingly timed to that year's Psyche theme. The piece was noted at the time as carrying "several levels of symbolism," though the specifics weren't recorded beyond that.

title: Rocker hand
imageAlt: Holographic sticker with rock devil horns hand gesture and Take Me Down to Black Rock City Where the Dust is Free text
description: “I woke up and somehow had the Guns & Roses song “Paradise City’ in my head and changed the lyrics wishing for “Home”. I thought it was catchy and knew everyone was and is longing for home” – Erin.

title: Gypsy Kitties Robo Brain Machina’
imageAlt: Dark blue circular sticker with glowing robotic cat design and Gypsy Kitties Robo Brain Machina Burning Man 2018 text
description: Another Gypsy Kitties camp sticker, created by fingerwave and gifted at the 2018 Burning Man event, playing on that year's I, Robot theme with its "Robo Brain Machina" name.

title: BRC Stamp
imageAlt: Postage stamp style sticker with illustrated Burning Man effigy tower, Forever text, and Black Rock City USA
description:
Postage stamps commemorate things worth remembering: people, places, moments in history. The BRC Stamp takes that format and applies it to Black Rock City — the temporary metropolis that rises and disappears each year in the Nevada desert. 2022 was a meaningful year to make this statement: the first full-scale in-person Burning Man since COVID canceled the event in 2020 and severely limited it in 2021.
A stamp says: this place is real, this moment is worth marking. Sticking it to something says: I was there, and I want the world to know it. The BRC Stamp does both at once, in miniature.

title: Da Vinci's Workshop
imageAlt: Circular Burning Man 2016 “Da Vinci’s Workshop” gate sticker with Renaissance sketches, gears, flowers, and blue MAN on black background.
description: This official Da Vinci's Workshop sticker was created by Rink for the 2016 Burning Man event, originally printed as a 4-inch round design and distributed by the Greeters at the gate.

description: Psych was contributed by David Silverman for the 2005 Burning Man event, playing on that year's official theme, Psyche.

description: Orange Man comes from Brain Freeze/Got Stickers camp, dated to the 2009 Burning Man event and that year's Evolution theme.

title: Whiskey & Dust Camp
imageAlt: Circular holographic sticker with illustrated female cyborg figure and geometric ring border, Whiskey and Dust Camp text
description: This Whiskey & Dust Camp sticker is an oil painting on board with digitally added lettering, designed by artist Marie Vlasic. Whiskey & Dust is a Colorado-based theme camp centered on whiskey education and yoga, established in 2009. This sticker is dated to the 2018 Burning Man event and that year's I, Robot theme.

title: We are everywhere
imageAlt: Black circular sticker with Burning Man Project logo and city skyline and We Are Everywhere burningmanproject.org text
description: We Are Everywhere was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2011 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Rites of Passage theme.

title: Fuck Your Burn
imageAlt: Rectangular sticker with the works "Fuck Your Burn" on a black background.
description: This sticker was submitted by Dima for the 2025 Burning Man event, held under that year's Tomorrow Today theme. Its original designer isn't known — if you recognize the artist, the site's contact form is the place to flag it.

title: Burning Man Information Radio
imageAlt: Round purple sticker with stylized BRC fertility figure and Welcome Home text, 2012 Burning Man camp badge
description:
Cool purple foil — probably our most popular of all the years we produced these, said the BMIR crew. The 2012 Burning Man theme was Fertility 2.0, arching above a bold BRC with Welcome Home! below. Part of BMIR's annual series of BRC oval camp giveaways, this one stands out for the reflective foil that makes it shimmer like a Playa mirage.
Of all the oval stickers BMIR produced across the years, this is the one people remember. The purple foil catches light differently than any other sticker in the series — the kind of detail that makes a small thing feel rare. Hard to miss on a bumper. Harder to forget.

title: Ranger Ralph’s Camp Six Sixty Six – CANCELED
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with ornate mandala design and CANCELLED red stamp overlaid and Camp Six Sixty Six Burning Man text
description: This companion sticker marks the cancellation of Ranger Ralph's Camp Six Sixty-Six's in-person plans for the 2020 Burning Man event, when Black Rock City's physical gathering was called off due to COVID-19 and reimagined as the virtual Multiverse. It was printed as a 5-inch holographic design, contributed by Ralph Boethling.

title: Domestic Entropy Reduction Team (DERT)
imageAlt: Dark square sticker with cartoon maid character and Domestic Entropy Reduction Team GM 13 text
description: This sticker represents the Domestic Entropy Reduction Team (DERT), a Burning Man theme camp, contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2013 event — the year of the festival's Cargo Cult theme.

title: You Might Not Be There Yet
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with cosmic space imagery and person reaching toward stars, You Might Not Be There Yet text
description: This sticker was given away by Sergi Villacampa at the 2022 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Waking Dreams theme.

title: Bunny Camp
imageAlt: Dark blue circular sticker with Bunny Camp 2000 text in simple bold design
description:
The year 2000 was the year of The Body — Burning Man's theme that year explored the human form as art, as vessel, as something to celebrate and challenge. Bunny Camp arrived in that context, which tells you something about the energy of the camp even if the name alone doesn't reveal everything.
This is the earliest Bunny Camp sticker in the catalog — the 2000 edition, the origin point of a three-year run that would continue through 2001 and 2003. A camp that keeps printing stickers is a camp that keeps coming back, and a camp that keeps coming back is one people genuinely love.

title: Taosyty
imageAlt: Yellow square sticker with Native American Zia sun symbol and Taosyty 2003 text
description: Taosyty was contributed by Harlan Gruber for the 2003 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Beyond Belief theme. No further details about the piece's design or origin are recorded.

title: BMIR
imageAlt: Orange circular sticker with radio DJ headphones illustration and BMIR 94.5 FM The Voice of the Man text
description:
BMIR 94.5 FM is Burning Man's official Playa radio station, founded in 2000 by Carmen Mauk.
Broadcasting live from Black Rock City, it delivers event logistics, weather, music, and interviews during the event week. This 2010 sticker marks the year BMIR began 24-hour live broadcasting.

title: Exodus
imageAlt: Teal rectangular sticker with EXODUS text in bold decorative lettering with circular X design
description: This sticker was made for the Exodus crew, the volunteers who manage the multi-hour vehicle exit from Black Rock City at the close of the event. Contributed by Ranger OdWally, it's dated to the 2004 Burning Man event, held under that year's Vault of Heaven theme.

title: HOT COCO
imageAlt: Dark sticker with flaming Burning Man effigy and Hot Coco Black Rock City MMXXII text
description: This sticker represents Hot Coco, a Burning Man theme camp, created by Jason Wasabi for the 2012 event — the year of the festival's Fertility 2.0 theme.

title: Star Dust Man
imageAlt: Pastel gradient sticker with Burning Man X-figure silhouette and You Are Made of Star Dust text
description: Star Dust Man was created by Jennifer Taylor (Fluffy) for the 2022 Burning Man event, with the line "we are made of star dust." It arrived during the year of the festival's Waking Dreams theme.

title: Radical Indulgence
imageAlt: Black rectangular sticker with bold bright red Radical Self Indulgence text
description: Radical Indulgence was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2012 Burning Man event, named in the spirit of Burning Man's Ten Principles — a wink at "radical self-expression" filtered through that year's Fertility 2.0 theme.

title: Cabana Club
imageAlt: Teal square sticker with palm tree silhouettes and Burning Man figure and Cabana Club text
description: Cabana Club was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2013 Burning Man event, the year of the festival's Cargo Cult theme.

title: Shelf Bombers

description: This is the sticker awarded to Soup Warriors in the Default when they place a relabeled can of soup on a shelf and post a pic. A Camp Balls Soup Can Patch is also awarded. To date over 100 Shelf Bombers have placed soup.

title: United We Burn Together
imageAlt: Holographic sticker with rows of blue portable toilets and text “United — We Burn Together” and “BRC 2025 Rewards.”
description: This sticker, "United We Burn Together," was submitted by Dima for the 2025 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Tomorrow Today theme. Specific design details haven't been documented yet.

title: Man Timeline
imageAlt: Wide rectangular sticker with green Metropolis Burning Man 2010 timeline and human figure silhouettes along bottom
description: Man Timeline 2010 was contributed by Steven Fritz for the Metropolis-themed 2010 Burning Man event.

title: Metropolis
imageAlt: Dark square sticker with art deco Burning Man figure in circular frame and Metropolis II MMX text
description: Metropolis II was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2010 Burning Man event, continuing the Metropolis series named for that year's theme.

title: Camp Balls - Soup Can Label
imageAlt: Wide rectangular red and white Camp Balls soup can label sticker with Checkin Noods Hoop text
description:
This is the 2020 version of the Camp Balls Soup Can Label, mailed out by the thousands to Burners in Defaultica, to anyone who asks for a couple (one to keep, one to shelf bomb with). 
When the pic is posted of the relabeled soup can on a shelf, a Shelf Bomber sticker and Camp Balls Soup Can Patch are awarded.

title: Azul
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with geometric sigil symbols arranged in circle and tribal script around border
description:
The 2003 Burning Man theme "Beyond Belief" invited participants into the space between reverence and ridicule — to play with sacred imagery without being bound by dogma.
Azul means blue in Spanish and Portuguese — a color long associated in many traditions with the mystical, the divine, and the liminal. In the context of Beyond Belief, a name like Azul is not incidental: it points toward something oceanic, something you can reach into but never fully grasp.
It's the kind of artifact that seems designed to be found rather than explained, a small talisman for the bewildered and the curious. Bryan Dongray contributed it to the Archive in 2003.

title: Pyro Boy
imageAlt: Yellow and black square sticker with cartoon fire performer and Pyro Boy pyroboy.com text
description: Pyro Boy was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2012 Burning Man event, the year of the festival's Fertility 2.0 theme.

title: Peace & Nudity
imageAlt: Dark square sticker with large white Peace and Nudity text and Burning Man figure
description: Peace & Nudity was contributed by Bob Parker for the 2001 Burning Man event, the year the festival's official theme was Seven Ages. The name pairs two ideas long associated with Black Rock City's culture of radical self-expression.

title: Ice Cave
imageAlt: Dark square sticker with black and white tribal butterfly moth design and Ice Cave text
description: Ice Cave was created by Margo for the 2019 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Metamorphoses theme.

title: I Have Seen The Future
imageAlt: Vintage-style poster with eyes above a crystal ball showing flames, text reads “I have seen the future — Burning Man Black Rock City 2025.”

title: ATABEY
imageAlt: White square sticker with intricate black linework deity face and Atabey Burning Man Matriarcas 2022 text
description:
ATABEY was a 2022 Burning Man Honoraria installation by Puerto Rican artist NiNo — the same creator who brought the beloved MÚCARO wooden owl to the Playa.
Built from repurposed steel and recycled silver pizza pans, ATABEY depicted the Taíno goddess of the earth and freshwater in monumental form.
A deep-Playa piece, ATABEY glowed from across the flat desert like a signal fire.

title: Playa to Playa
imageAlt: White circular sticker with blue Burning Man figure icon and Playa to Playa text
description: Created by Carla for Playa to Playa camp, this sticker carries the line "playa to playa, player to player" for the 2025 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Tomorrow Today theme.

title: I Bitched At Burning Man
imageAlt: Sticker: orange 'I BITCHED AT BURNING MAN' around a tree design with a sun, spirals, flames, on charcoal. Below: 'Dept. of Whining & Playa Relations.
description: Created by Joe Aiello as part of 'Fuck Yer Burn Complaint Box,' an art project sited at 1:15 and the Trash Fence. This sticker was affixed to the back of the project's own complaint form, gifted as a souvenir to anyone who made the trek out to file one. Several complainers, notably, didn't bother taking their sticker.

title: Sacred Cow
imageAlt: Dark shield shaped sticker with sacred cow illustration in flames and Sacred Cow text in Arabic and English
description:
The Sacred Cow sticker comes from 2018, the year Burning Man's official theme was I, Robot — an exploration of humanity's uneasy relationship with artificial intelligence, automation, and the question of what, if anything, still separates a person from a machine. 
Made by Clark for the camp of the same name, the sticker shares its title with an old idiom: a "sacred cow" is an idea or tradition treated as too revered to question, a phrase rooted in the reverence cows are given in Hindu tradition. It's a fitting name to bring to a year built around asking uncomfortable questions about what people take for granted — about technology, and about themselves. 
It's also a small piece of playa history in its own right: proof that this crew claimed a spot in Black Rock City in 2018 and gave away a bit of their own irreverence for free.

title: Axis Mundi — Green
imageAlt: Circular sticker: a kaleidoscope mandala in blues, pinks, yellows, greens, oranges, green border. Text: Burning Man 2026, Axis Mundi, Black Rock City.
description: Clark Stoeckley designed this mandala series for 2026, channeling the Burning Man theme's "cosmic, centering energy" into Islamic geometry-inspired patterns. He gifted 500 sticker packs — these mandalas paired with humorous and political stickers — to burners across Black Rock City, calling the reactions when people opened them one of his favorite moments of the Burn. Stoeckley is a repeat Burning Man muralist (work on the playa in 2009, 2010, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2022, and 2024) and a longtime geometric abstract painter, currently an Associate Professor of Art & Graphic Design at the American University of Kuwait.

title: Radical Ritual
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with mandala ornate design in red and green tones and Radical Ritual Burning Man 2017 text
description: “Official” version of my (Ralph Boethling) 2017 Radical Ritual sticker design, “we like your sticker; your words not so much. can you take off your words and make ours bigger?”

title: My Life is a Theme Camp
imageAlt: Aerial photograph sticker of RV camp scene with My Life is a Theme Camp Burning Man 2014 text
description: "My Life Is a Theme Camp" was created by squishelle for the 2014 Burning Man event, also printed in a run of 400, during that year's Caravansary theme.

title: The Burning Woman
imageAlt: Round sticker with illustrated dancing woman holding umbrella in colorful pattern and The Burning Woman 2021 text
description: Created by Stephen Blake, this sticker was described by its contributor as a tribute to a Banksy artwork known as "The Burning Woman." It's dated to the 2021 Burning Man event, the second consecutive year Black Rock City's gathering moved online, themed The Great Unknown.

title: Flock of Donkeys
imageAlt: Dark sticker with bold distressed white Stupid Dirt Rave text and small skull icons
description: This sticker was given out at Flock of Donkeys theme camp and contributed by Alejandro Vizio, dated to the 2024 Burning Man event and that year's Curiouser & Curiouser theme.

title: Animalia
imageAlt: Holographic circular Burning Man sticker reading “Animalia 2023,” with the Man symbol and reflective rainbow foil surface.
description:
The Man — arms raised, the same silhouette burning at the heart of Black Rock City on Saturday night no matter what that year's theme is. This sticker breaks that rule on purpose. 
For 2023's Animalia theme, Dima swapped the Man's head for a cat's, a small artistic edit that makes literal what the theme itself was arguing: that humans are animals too, not separate from the kingdom but part of it. It's playful theme commentary dressed up as tribute art, rounding out a trio with their wolf and cat-face designs from the same year.

title: Playa Time
imageAlt: Brown circular sticker with compass clock design and Core 2017 DMV Playa Time text
description: Playa Time was a 20-foot human-powered cuckoo clock built by Vancouver's Burning Man regional community as its contribution to CORE (the Circle of Regional Effigies), a collaborative project bringing effigies from multiple regional Burning Man communities to the 2011 event, staged under that year's Rites of Passage theme.

title: Larry And the 10 Principles
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with Larry Harvey portrait in center surrounded by the 10 Burning Man principles written in arc
description: Larry and the 10 Principles was created by Jamen Percy, a longtime Burner later invited to join Burning Man's official documentation team, for the 2018 event, honoring Burning Man co-founder Larry Harvey and the Ten Principles he articulated to describe the community's core values. It arrived during the year of the festival's I, Robot theme.

title: Funtown sticker
imageAlt: Colorful sticker with cartoon devil figure and Funtown 2014 Ill Ville at Burning Man text
description:
This sticker was created by Sandy and contributed by George for Illumination Village, one of Black Rock City's oldest theme camps — founded in 1995 with about 30 members and grown to roughly 200 today. Over the decades its resident artists have produced more than 400 works displayed on the playa, and the village is recognized as the birthplace of the art collective Flaming Lotus Girls.
This particular sticker, based on a photo taken at the 2013 event, was made for Illumination Village's presence at the 2014 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Caravansary theme.

title: Inner Rim Liquors
imageAlt: Rectangular sticker with Inner Rim Liquors in retro 70s lettering with flame logo and Burning Man text
description: Inner Rim Liquors was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2011 Burning Man event, the year of the festival's Rites of Passage theme.

title: I Pooped in a Bucket
imageAlt: White square sticker with bucket cartoon and I Pooped in a Bucket BRC 2021 Plan B Renegade Burn Free Burn text in humorous style
description:
I Pooped In A Bucket is a 2021 Burning Man sticker from GYST — Get Your Shit Together — the playa's own food-scrap composting and waste-management camp.
A bucket is genuinely how a lot of campers handle theirs without plumbing. GYST leaned into the joke, in the spirit of radical self-reliance.

title: Rock Art
imageAlt: Dark blue sticker with stylized bird illustration and 09 Burning Man text in bold yellow
description: Rock Art was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2009 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Evolution theme — a nod, perhaps, to some of humanity's oldest evolutionary evidence of art-making.

title: Bioluminescent Slug
imageAlt: Dark sticker with glowing blue eye motif and Bioluminescent Slug High Maintenance Camp text
description:
A great poofer, by all accounts.
The Bioluminescent Slug is a mutant vehicle that rolled onto the Playa starting in 2008 and kept going through 2022 — nearly fifteen years of glowing, fire-breathing slug action on the Nevada desert. Poofers are art cars equipped to shoot large bursts of propane flame, and this one did it while built to look like the world's most bioluminescent gastropod.
The sticker from 2016 is a piece of a long, weird, wonderful story.

title: Bunny Camp
imageAlt: Pink circular sticker with Bunny Camp 2001 text, 3:30 and the Lover subtitle, and stylized figure
description:
Bunny Camp is one of those long-running Burning Man camps whose sticker archive tells a story across multiple years — 2000, 2001, 2003. The 2001 sticker arrived during the Seven Ages theme, a year when Burning Man explored the stages of a human life from birth to old age and the rites that mark each passage.
What exactly happens at Bunny Camp has always been part of the mystique — the best camps at Burning Man protect their secrets a little. What's clear is that enough people cared enough to print stickers three years running, which in BRC terms is as close to an institution as it gets.

title: Camp Yes Please
imageAlt: Illustrated sticker with anime-style winged woman in dramatic sky setting, Camp Yes Please theme
description: Camp Yes Please's 2006 sticker poses its own question right in the design — "Who is Camp Yes Please and what do they do?" Beyond the camp's name and that year's Hope and Fear theme, no further details are recorded.

title: Black Rock City Biergarten
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with vintage biergarten illustration and Black Rock Biergarten Burning Man 2004 text
description:
In the middle of the Nevada desert, in the middle of one of the world's most ambitious temporary cities, someone decided to build a German beer garden.
That is the Black Rock City Biergarten. The 2004 Burning Man theme was Vault of Heaven — celestial, cosmic, full of stars and mystery. And right there on the Playa was a camp serving cold beer in a biergarten.
The audacity. The logic. The fact that it worked completely — because everything works at Burning Man if you commit to the bit.

title: Gypsy Kitties Anubis Afterlife Lounge
imageAlt: Circular sticker with Egyptian Anubis cat design in colorful style and Gypsy Kitties Anubis Afterlife Lounge text
description: This Gypsy Kitties camp sticker, themed around an "Anubis Afterlife Lounge," was gifted at the 2017 Burning Man event — more than 200 were handed out that year, which was staged under the festival's Radical Ritual theme.

BMIR — Burning Man Information Radio — has broadcast live from Black Rock City on 94.5 FM since founder Carmen Mauk launched it in 2000. 
This 2013 sticker was a shiny giveaway design by BMIR staffers Bobzilla, Lisa Marie, and eyefleye, handed out on the playa.

title: El Swear – Potato
imageAlt: Square sticker with photograph of a potato and Potato Burning Man 2017 text in humorous style
description: El Swear - Potato, created by Lofax, was named the Best Sticker of 2017 by the site's organizers, arriving during the year of Burning Man's Radical Ritual theme.

title: Spire of Fire
imageAlt: Dark sticker with stylized phoenix fire bird design and The Spire of Fire 2010 text
description:
The Spire of Fire is a recurring large-scale fire art installation at Burning Man — a towering structure that concentrates and channels fire at height. The 2010 version appeared during the "Metropolis: The Life of Cities" event year, a fitting context for something that functions as architecture: a landmark, a gathering point, something that orients people across the open Playa the way spires once oriented travelers across European landscapes.
The spire form has ancient precedents as a marker of significance — obelisks, minarets, steeples, towers. At Burning Man, the fire spire makes those references in a temporary medium: monumental and arresting while it burns, gone without trace when the event ends. That combination of grandeur and impermanence is central to Burning Man's aesthetic philosophy.
This sticker was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2010 event year.

title: Floating Man
imageAlt: Red square sticker with Burning Man stick figure in diving pose and 02 text in orange and red tones
description: Contributed by Peter Durand for the 2002 Burning Man event, this sticker ties directly into that year's official theme, The Floating World — the nautical concept that had the Man standing atop an 80-foot lighthouse and filled the playa with ship- and sea-creature-themed art and mutant vehicles.

title: Peace & Love
imageAlt: Dark sticker with ornate orange and yellow floral heart design and Burning Man 2005 Peace and Love theme
description: Peace and Love was contributed by Stacie Mishcon for the 2005 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Psyche theme.

title: We Are Everywhere
imageAlt: Holographic hexagonal sticker with We Are Everywhere text and Burning Man figure in iridescent rainbow finish
description: This Camp Decimation sticker was created by Larry DeVincenzi for the 2024 Burning Man event, signed off with "see you in the dust." It arrived during the year of the festival's Curiouser & Curiouser theme.

title: Battle Born Burners
imageAlt: Dark rectangular sticker with illustrated western frontier scene and Battle Born Burners Nevada cowboy theme
description:
Battle Born Burners has been on the Playa since 1994 — making them one of the oldest camps in Black Rock City, burning almost as long as Burning Man itself.
A vintage Nevada-themed bar and casino, they describe themselves as The Bar with Nevadatude and run the city's only casino operation. Mostly made up of Nevadans who are literally battle born (it's the state motto), this camp is a love letter to the Silver State planted square in the middle of the Black Rock Desert.
This 2022 sticker was designed by Hagen Sandoval.

title: iRobot Hand rise
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with mechanical robot hand rising and Black Rock City 2018 iRobot Hand Rise text
description: iRobot Hand Rise was created by Jamen Percy, a longtime Burner and aerial photographer later invited onto Burning Man's official documentation team, for the 2018 event, again drawing on that year's I, Robot theme.

title: Flaming Lotus Girls
imageAlt: Dark diamond-shaped sticker with flame lotus design and Flaming Lotus Girls text in white
description: This sticker represents Flaming Lotus Girls, the all-women fire arts collective, and references Noetica, their 2017 Burning Man Honorarium sculpture — two sets of stainless steel squares, one hydraulically powered by the other. It arrived during the year of the festival's Radical Ritual theme.

title: MÚCARO
imageAlt: Black sticker with detailed white owl illustration and Mucaro Burning Man Honoraria 2017 text
description:
This is another amazing art project from the artist NiNo. The creator of "ATABEY" the oversized fish in 2022 and the giant frame "GOT FRAMED" that debuted  2015.
MÚCARO was a 30-foot interactive owl sculpture by Puerto Rican artist El NiNo, installed at Burning Man 2017. Visitors climbed spiral stairs up into its head and looked out through giant rotating eyes across the Playa. The owl honors the Múcaro — a screech owl sacred to the Taíno indigenous people, with petroglyphs carved in Puerto Rican caves dating to the 13th century. El NiNo dedicated it to his mother, a teacher for over 45 years, and became the first Puerto Rican artist to receive a Black Rock City Honoraria grant.

description: Another Gypsy Kitties camp sticker, created by fingerwave and gifted at the 2015 Burning Man event, held under that year's Carnival of Mirrors theme.

imageAlt: Gold and dark circular sticker with art deco Burning Man figure in ornate decorative frame and Metropolis Burning Man text
description: One of several stickers from the 2010 Burning Man theme 'Metropolis: The Life of Cities,' conceived by Larry Harvey. BRC streets were named after world cities from Athens to Kyoto. The event was marked by a historic rainstorm that flooded the playa and briefly shut down all roads.

title: Burners Unite - We will burn again!
imageAlt: Round white sticker with orange flame and Burners Unite We Will Burn Again text in black
description:
The companion sticker to Burners Unite, also created for the Can't Find My Way Home Facebook gift exchange during the COVID years. Where Burners Unite is a statement of solidarity, We Will Burn Again is a promise. A declaration that the cancellation is temporary. That the city will return. That the people will find each other again in the dust.
It did return. But in 2021, when this was made, that was not yet certain — and this sticker was made anyway. Certainty is not required for commitment. Burning Man has always been about showing up for something before you know exactly what it will be. We Will Burn Again is that energy, applied to a global pandemic.

title: Ranger Ralph’s Camp Six Sixty Six
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with ornate mandala design and Camp Six Sixty Six The Multiverse Burning Man 2020 text
description: Contributed by Ralph Boethling, this sticker welcomed participants to "Ranger Ralph's Camp Six Sixty-Six" for the 2020 Burning Man event — the year the in-person gathering was replaced by the virtual Multiverse event — printed as a 5-inch holographic design.

title: Dusty Gift
imageAlt: Black and white sticker reading "Axis Mundi, We Will Dance Again, 2026" with a QR code and "@dusty.gift, Follow us" printed on the edge.
description: "We Will Dance Again" was created by @dusty.gift for the 2026 Burning Man event, staged under that year's official Axis Mundi theme. @dusty.gift describes their work as "crafting magic for Playa" — handmade gifts and treasures made for the desert community.

title: BM Power Flower
imageAlt: Dark sticker with subtle circular power flower mandala design in deep tones
description:
Power Flower arrived at the 2017 Burning Man, the year of Radical Ritual — a theme exploring ceremony, worship, and the rites people create around meaning.
The sticker is a straightforward declaration: fire and the man, forever. At Burning Man this is not hyperbole. The combination of flower, fire, and the iconic Man figure distills something essential about what the event is — a ritual that regenerates itself every year, in the same place, with the same bonfire at its center.
With fire. Forever.

title: Lamplighters
imageAlt: Black-and-white sticker with lantern logo and text “Lamplighters,” “Illumination Navigation Celebration,” and “5pm Center Camp.”
description:
Learn about the Lamplighters. 
Do you have information about this sticker? If you do, please use the Contact Form (opens in new tab) to comment. Thanks, fingerwave.

title: Bee
imageAlt: Dark rectangular sticker with large yellow bee illustration and Burning Man Fertility 2.0 text with radiating sunburst
description:
The 2012 Burning Man theme, "Fertility 2.0," explored what it means to create in the digital age — a riff on the tech term "Web 2.0," it asked whether the internet was fertile ground, whether digital connectivity could generate culture, community, and meaning the way organic systems generate life. The theme pressed on a question many were beginning to feel acutely in 2012: was technology enriching human creativity, or beginning to replace it?
The bee is an almost irresistible symbol for Burning Man: a highly organized cooperative community that builds complex structures through collective labor, operates without centralized command, and exists in service of the hive's collective survival. Bees are also the essential agents of biological fertility — pollinators without whom most flowering plants cannot reproduce. Placing the bee at the center of a "Fertility 2.0" sticker ties these threads together: the organic and the social, the biological and the communal.
This sticker was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2012 event year.

title: Video Bleep

title: Kathy Kamp
imageAlt: Black sticker with white bold I Burned at Kathy Kamp text
description: Kathy Kamp was created as a dedication to Katherine Lampman, contributed by Jim Crupi for the 2004 Burning Man event, held under that year's Vault of Heaven theme.

title: Art Everywhere
imageAlt: Colorful sticker with abstract radio tower art and Art Everywhere BlackRockArts.org text in bold multicolor typography
description:
The Black Rock Arts Foundation (BRAF) is the nonprofit organization that grew out of Burning Man's commitment to supporting public art beyond the Playa. Founded to provide grants, education, and advocacy for public art in communities year-round, BRAF extends the Burning Man ethos outward — the conviction that transformative art should not be locked behind museum walls or limited to those who can afford access.
The "Art Everywhere" campaign this sticker promotes captured a core Burning Man belief: that art belongs in public space, that it should interrupt everyday life and be impossible to ignore. The transmission tower imagery suggests art as broadcast — signals reaching outward from a central source, finding people who might never come to the Playa but whose environments could still be shaped by the same spirit.
Contributed by Steven Fritz in 2012, during the "Fertility 2.0" event year, this sticker links the theme's emphasis on creative generation to BRAF's mission of seeding public art across communities far from Black Rock City.

title: Hyperbolic Immersion
imageAlt: White circular sticker with intricate mathematical hyperbolic tiling pattern and Burning Man 2003 Hyperbolic Immersion text
description: Hyperbolic Immersion was contributed by Zack Treisman for the 2003 Burning Man event, held under that year's Beyond Belief theme. No further details about the piece's design or origin are recorded.

title: I Robot - 2018
imageAlt: Circular Burning Man 2018 “I, Robot” gate sticker with neon green circuitry and pink flowers on a black background.
description: This sticker, created by Rink, was based directly on Burning Man's 2018 official theme, I, Robot.

title: Playa Dreamin'
imageAlt: White rectangular sticker with reclining figure silhouette and Playa Dreamin BRC 2008 text
description:
"Playa Dreamin'" is a play on "California Dreamin'" — the Mamas & the Papas song from 1965 that became an anthem of West Coast longing and the countercultural promise of California. Where the original song imagines escape to California's warmth, this sticker redirects that longing toward the Black Rock Desert: the dream has shifted from California's sunshine to the austere, otherworldly landscape of Nevada's high desert.
The 2008 Burning Man theme was "American Dream" — an exploration of what the American promise has meant and what it has failed to deliver. "Playa Dreamin'" participates in that critique: for many in the Burning Man community, the California dream has been complicated by commodification and celebrity culture, and the Playa has become the place where a different dream — of authentic community, radical creativity, and temporary freedom — remains possible.
This sticker was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2008 event year.

title: Stay At Home Camp
imageAlt: Brown circular sticker with wood grain cross-section ring design and 2020 Beyond the Known World text
description: Created by Steve for Stay At Home Camp, this design overlays Black Rock City's street map onto a photograph of a flower growing in his own front yard — a fitting image for the 2020 Burning Man event, held virtually as the Multiverse after the in-person gathering was cancelled.

title: Cryptomeria
imageAlt: Circular sticker: a spiral wood tower topped by a glowing blue figure with raised arms, under an aurora sky. Text: Burning Man 2026, Axis Mundi.
description:
This sticker, created by Burning Man artist Chad Rice, depicts Cryptomeria, the 2026 Man Pavilion designed by Alexander (Zander) Rose — the timber structure built to support that year's Man effigy. 
Rose based the design on Japan's Jōmon Sugi, an ancient cedar on Yakushima Island estimated at 2,170 to 7,200 years old, rendering a tree at architectural scale with dual interlocking spiral staircases that form a double-helix rising 60 feet to the Man's base.

title: Axis Mundi Swings
imageAlt: Round sticker showing two gold figures on swings beneath a red-columned pergola. Axis Mundi Swings · 40th Burning Man 2026 · Sophie Graubner Art
description:
AXIS MUNDI SWINGS is Sophie Graubner’s design for Burning Man 2026. 
This year’s theme, *Axis Mundi*, alludes—among other things—to the interconnectedness of all things. Sophie Graubner hails from Hamburg, Germany, and thus from Europe. Her concept envisions people sitting or standing on the swings, elevated in the air, where they can reflect on their own roots amidst the European heritage of Knossos.

Sophie Graubner plans to bring this design to Burning Man as a sculpture one day.

imageAlt: Sticker showing a fairy shrimp with wings and wand in a tutu, surrounded by text “The Playa Provides – Make a Wish – Fairy Shrimp Fairy.”
description: This sticker, "Make A Wish," was submitted by Dima for the 2025 Burning Man event, staged under that year's Tomorrow Today theme. Specific design details haven't been documented yet.

imageAlt: Illustrated sticker with serpent candle and spiral design and The Spire of Fire BRC text
description: Spire of Fire was contributed by Steven Fritz for the 2013 Burning Man event, the year of the festival's Cargo Cult theme.

title: You Are Good
imageAlt: Military camouflage helmet sticker with peace sign and You Are Good text
description: You Are Good is a veterans collective working to connect veterans and military families in the burner community, create art, and further advocate for mental health for all. Check out youaregoodprjct

title: Dream Camp
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with astronaut illustration and Dream Camp 2005 Esplanade giamind.com text
description: Dream Camp's 2005 sticker, contributed by Skyhawk, was made as a tribute to a sculpture by Pepe Ozan, one of Burning Man's best-known large-scale sculptors and fire-opera creators. It arrived during the year of the festival's Psyche theme.

title: Temple of Flux
imageAlt: Black square sticker with white abstract line drawing of radiating architectural beams forming a starburst, with text "Temple of Flux"
description:
Temple of Flux was Burning Man's official temple for 2010 — the Metropolis theme year — commissioned by Burning Man and designed by Jessica Hobbs, Rebecca Anders, and Peter Kimelman of the Flux Foundation. It was the first non-traditional temple design in Burning Man history.
Drawing from the canyonlands of the American Southwest, the structure rose from the Black Rock Desert floor as five massive double-curved walls — smooth, dune-like forms 190 feet long, 110 feet wide, and 40 feet tall. Built from wood and mild steel, the walls stood in an overlapping linear layout, creating a series of canyon-like passages and cave-like spaces that opened from all sides. Oriented to the arc of the sun and moon, angled fissures in the wall faces channeled changing light throughout the day. At night, illuminated from within, the structure shifted — what looked like earth and stone became burning embers, shadows dancing across the surfaces. The Temple of Flux burned at the close of the event, as all Burning Man temples do.

title: BMIR KOME
imageAlt: Orange circular sticker with radio DJ headphones illustration and BMIR 94.5 FM The Voice of the Man text
description:
Rocky's annual BMIR sticker series celebrates the great, weird, irreverent radio stations of American history — and KOME 98.5 FM was one of the best.
KOME broadcast from San Jose, California from 1971 to 1998, building a devoted South Bay rock audience through irreverence, raunchy humor, and freeform music programming that eventually got reined in by corporate consultants in 1982. Its stickers were on high school lockers across the Bay Area.
Pairing KOME with BMIR makes complete sense: two stations that earned their loyalty.

title: BRC - Greeters Camp
imageAlt: Dark circular sticker with red BRC text surrounded by orange flames and burningman.com text
description:
The Greeters are the first people you meet when you enter Black Rock City. Exuberantly costumed, wackily attired (or sometimes not attired at all), they welcome every participant with a booming Welcome home! — a tradition that started in the early days of Burning Man and has become one of its most enduring rituals.
By 2003, the Greeters were organized enough to run on-Playa training, help theme camp residents find their spots, and distribute maps, camera tags, and answers.
The sticker is their badge. You earned it by arriving.

title: Namaste Motherfucker
imageAlt: Green rectangular sticker with Namaste Motherfucker text in stylized font with Devanagari script
description: Namaste Motherfucker was created by Dave Aiazzi for Religion by Day, a Burning Man theme camp, during the 2003 event's Beyond Belief theme year. The name plays on the collision of reverent and irreverent language that runs through much of Black Rock City's humor — a sincere spiritual gesture delivered with a deliberately profane punchline.

title: Ranger Tested
imageAlt: Ranger Tested sticker. Yellow diamond. Text: Ranger Tested, Ranger Approved. Black Rock Rangers insignia — stylized winged figure. Burning Man 2012.
description:
The Black Rock Rangers have been navigating the edge of chaos at Burning Man since 1992.
Not cops, not security — volunteer community mediators who walk and ride the streets of Black Rock City day and night in pairs, ready to resolve conflict, provide information, and connect participants with whatever they need. If something goes sideways on the Playa, a Ranger is who you want to find.
This sticker, contributed by Steven Fritz in 2012, carries the unofficial seal of approval: if it's Ranger Tested, you know it holds up out there.

title: Spire of Fire
imageAlt: Colorful sticker with red orange and blue triangular spire design and geometric tribal pattern
description:
The Spire of Fire was a large-scale art installation at the 2013 Burning Man event — a towering structure designed to channel and display fire at height, making it visible across the open Playa. Large-scale fire art has been central to Burning Man's identity since the earliest events, and spire or tower structures are among the most arresting forms that tradition has taken.
The 2013 "Cargo Cult" theme asked participants to examine what objects contain, what rituals accomplish, and how value is constructed through ceremony and belief. A towering column of fire is one of humanity's oldest and most universal ceremonial symbols — fire raised on high has marked sacred sites, guided travelers, and signified divine presence across countless cultures for millennia. The spire makes that ancient language available to the temporary city on the Playa.
This sticker, the first of two Spire of Fire stickers from 2013, was contributed by Steven Fritz for that event year.

title: BM2020 #Never4get
imageAlt: Rectangular sticker with Burning Man 2020 Never4get text in neon graffiti lettering on dark background
description:
An imaginary sixth grader designed their first Burning Man sticker. That is the premise, and it is perfect.
The year was 2020. Burning Man was canceled. A real adult designed a sticker from the perspective of a kid who just discovered the event and immediately had strong feelings about losing it to a pandemic.
The result is earnest, slightly absurd, and completely correct. BM2020 Never4get is the kind of protest art that understands its own joke without stopping being sincere about it.

title: Laocoon’s Timetable
imageAlt: Square sticker with Burning Man 2025 Tomorrow Today design and photo collage of playa art installations
description:
This Burning Man 2025 sticker, titled "Laocoon’s Timetable," blends mythology, evolution, and futurism into a symbolic visual narrative. At its heart is the Laocoön Group sculpture, representing humanity’s timeless struggle against fate and divine forces. Surrounding it, jellyfish drift through a cosmic sky, symbolizing our ancient biological origins and the fluid, adaptive nature of life.
Set against the Nevada mountains of Black Rock Desert, the artwork grounds its mythological themes in the real-world landscape of Burning Man. The white Burning Man effigy stands as a modern beacon of transformation and ritual, merging classical and futuristic forms. The phrase “Tomorrow Today” urges immediate action, reflection, and evolution in both spirit and society.

title: Burnycorn
imageAlt: Circular sticker. Unicorn split: flaming mane on left (day), crescent moon and stars on right (night). Rainbow horn. Burning Man 2022 Waking Dreams.
description:
"This little unicorn is in a Waking Dream embracing the surreal". — Wendy. 
Camp Corny (@campcorny) has been bringing unicorn energy to Black Rock City for years — a dance camp with a unicorn arch, spirit animal adoptions, and a dedicated following on the Playa. Their 2022 sticker, known as the BurnyCorn, captures their whole identity in one image: a unicorn that is equal parts fire and stardust, day and night, Playa absurdism and genuine magic.
2022 was Burning Man's Waking Dreams year — a theme about the blur between dreaming and waking consciousness, and transforming inner visions into something real. Camp Corny leaned into it perfectly. A unicorn that burns by day and chases stars by night is exactly the kind of creature that only exists in a waking dream. The BurnyCorn was theirs to keep.

That year's theme, Seven Ages, cast the entire event as a giant board game: participants moved through seven symbolic life stages — the Cradle, Playground, Chapel, Coliseum, Temple of Wisdom, Maze, and Mausoleum — in pursuit of wisdom through choice, striving, trial, and transformation.

title: Bad Edcuation
imageAlt: ticker advertising “Coffee and Croissants” at Camp Bad Education, showing a heart-shaped sunrise, croissant, and smiling coffee cup character.
description:
Bad Education is a Burning Man camp built on community, creativity, and a little bit of mischief.
Run by a leadership team called The School Board and guided by a philosophy they call The Way to BE, this 2025 camp set up at 2:30 & Bradbury and brought a family-forged-in-dust energy that earned them a clean MOOP Map. They paneled at the official Burning Man Camp Symposium and left the Playa better than they found it.
Bad Education: where the lessons are good and the classroom is made of dust.
